title.zh: 卷三百二十 列傳第二百〇八 外國一 朝鮮
title.raw: 卷三百二十 列傳第二百〇八 外國一 朝鮮 Volume 320 Biographies 208: Foreign States 1: Korea

sentences.zh: 朝鮮，箕子所封國也。

translations.literal: Korea was the state enfeoffed to Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: Korea was the kingdom granted to Jizi as his fief.

sentences.zh: 漢以前曰朝鮮。

translations.literal: Before the Han it was called Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Han dynasty it was known as Joseon.

sentences.zh: 始為燕人衛滿所據，漢武帝平之，置真番、臨屯、樂浪、玄菟四郡。

translations.literal: Initially it was occupied by Wei Man, a man of Yan; Emperor Wu of Han pacified it and established the four commanderies of Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: At first it fell under the control of Wei Man from Yan; Emperor Wu of Han conquered the region and established the four commanderies of Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 漢末，有扶余人高氏據其地，改國號曰高麗，又曰高句麗，居平壤，即樂浪也。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, a man of Fuyu of the Gao clan seized the territory, changed the state name to Gaoli, also called Gaogouli, with its seat at Pyongyang, which was Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Han, a man of Fuyu named Gao took the land, renamed the state Goryeo (also called Goguryeo), and established his capital at Pyongyang—the former Lelang commandery.

sentences.zh: 已，為唐所破，東徙。

translations.literal: Later it was defeated by Tang and moved east.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Tang forces broke the kingdom, and it shifted eastward.

sentences.zh: 後唐時，王建代高氏，兼併新羅、百濟地，徙居松岳，曰東京，而以平壤為西京。

translations.literal: During Later Tang, Wang Jian replaced the Gao clan, annexed the lands of Silla and Baekje, moved to Songak and called it the Eastern Capital, while making Pyongyang the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Tang period, Wang Geon supplanted the Gao line, absorbed the territories of Silla and Baekje, moved his seat to Songak and called it the Eastern Capital, while keeping Pyongyang as the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 其國北鄰契丹，西則女直，南曰日本，元至元中，西京內屬，置東甯路總管府，盡慈嶺為界。

translations.literal: Its state bordered Khitan to the north, Jurchen to the west, and Japan to the south. In the middle of the Yuan Zhiyuan era, the Western Capital was incorporated and the Dongning Circuit Administration Office was established, with Jichiling as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom lay adjacent to the Khitan in the north, the Jurchen in the west, and Japan to the south. In the Zhiyuan period of Yuan, the Western Capital was brought under direct rule and the Dongning Circuit Administration Office was established, with Jichiling as the border.

sentences.zh: 明興，王高麗者王顓。

translations.literal: When the Ming arose, the ruler of Goryeo was Wang Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty rose, Goryeo was ruled by King Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位之元年遣使賜璽書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Taizu's accession, he sent envoys bearing an imperial seal letter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year after the founding emperor took the throne, he dispatched envoys with an imperial letter bearing the seal.

sentences.zh: 二年送還其國流人。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned exiles of their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent back refugees from their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 顓表賀，貢方物，且請封。

translations.literal: Zhuan submitted a memorial of congratulations, presented local products, and requested enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan sent a memorial of congratulation, presented tribute goods, and asked to be invested with a title.

sentences.zh: 帝遣符璽郎偰斯齎詔及金印誥文封顓為高麗國王，賜曆及錦綺。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Seal Officer Qiesi bearing an edict and golden seal patent to enfeoff Zhuan as King of Goryeo, bestowing a calendar and brocade silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Seal Officer Qiesi with an edict and a patent of investiture on a golden seal, naming Zhuan King of Goryeo, and granted him an imperial calendar and brocade silks.

sentences.zh: 其秋，顓遣總部尚書成惟得、千牛衛大將軍金甲兩上表謝，並賀天壽節，因請祭服制度，帝命工部制賜之。

translations.literal: That autumn, Zhuan sent Director of the General Department Cheng Weide and General of the Thousand-Ox Guard Jin Jialiang to submit memorials of thanks, also congratulating the Emperor's birthday, and requesting the regulations for sacrificial robes; the Emperor ordered the Ministry of Works to manufacture and grant them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhuan sent Cheng Weide, Director of the General Department, and Jin Jialiang, General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, with memorials of thanks and congratulations on the emperor's birthday, and requested the prescribed form of sacrificial garments; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Works to prepare and bestow them.

sentences.zh: 惟得等辭歸，帝從容問：「王居國何為？

translations.literal: When Weide and the others took leave to return, the Emperor casually asked: "What does the king do in governing his state?
translations.idiomatic: As Weide and his party prepared to depart, the emperor casually inquired: "What does the king devote himself to in running his kingdom?

sentences.zh: 城郭修乎？

translations.literal: Are the walls and defenses maintained?
translations.idiomatic: Are his cities and fortifications kept in repair?

sentences.zh: 兵甲利乎？

translations.literal: Are weapons sharp?
translations.idiomatic: Are his arms and armor in good order?

sentences.zh: 宮室壯乎？」

translations.literal: Are palaces grand?"
translations.idiomatic: Are his palaces and halls built to proper splendor?"

sentences.zh: 頓首言：「東海波臣，惟知崇信釋氏，他未遑也。」

translations.literal: He kowtowed and said: "Your wave-bound subject east of the sea knows only to revere and believe in Buddhism; other matters he has not attended to."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and replied: "Your subject bounded by the eastern seas knows only to honor and worship the Buddha; he has had no leisure for anything else."

sentences.zh: 遂以書諭之曰：「古者王公設險，未嘗去兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon by letter he admonished him, saying: "In antiquity kings and dukes relied on natural barriers and never dispensed with military force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wrote to admonish him: "In antiquity kings and feudal lords relied on strategic terrain and never laid aside arms.

sentences.zh: 民以食為天，而國必有出政令之所。

translations.literal: The people take food as heaven, and a state must have a place from which to issue government orders.
translations.idiomatic: The people regard food as their heaven, and every state must have a seat from which to issue its commands.

sentences.zh: 今有人民而無城郭，人將何依？

translations.literal: Now there are people but no walls—where will the people rely?
translations.idiomatic: If you have subjects but no fortified cities, what will your people depend upon?

sentences.zh: 武備不修，則威弛；

translations.literal: If military preparations are not maintained, authority slackens;
translations.idiomatic: If martial readiness is neglected, your prestige will weaken;

sentences.zh: 地不耕，則民艱於食；

translations.literal: if land is not cultivated, the people will suffer hardship in food;
translations.idiomatic: if the fields lie fallow, your people will struggle for food;

sentences.zh: 且有居室，無廳事，無以示尊嚴。

translations.literal: moreover, to have living quarters but no audience hall shows no dignity.
translations.idiomatic: and to have dwelling chambers but no hall of audience is to show no dignity befitting a ruler.

sentences.zh: 此數者朕甚不取。

translations.literal: These several things I greatly disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: I find each of these practices deeply objectionable.

sentences.zh: 夫國之大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: The great business of a state lies in sacrifice and in arms.

sentences.zh: 苟闕斯二者，而徒事佛求福，梁武之事，可為明鑒。

translations.literal: If these two are lacking and one merely serves Buddhism seeking blessings, the affair of Liang Wudi can serve as a clear mirror.
translations.idiomatic: If you neglect these two and devote yourself only to Buddhism in pursuit of merit, the example of Emperor Wu of Liang stands as a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 王國北接契丹、女直，而南接倭，備禦之道，王其念之。」

translations.literal: Your kingdom borders Khitan and Jurchen to the north and Wō to the south; methods of defense—your majesty should consider them."
translations.idiomatic: Your kingdom adjoins the Khitan and Jurchen in the north and the Japanese in the south; you would do well to give careful thought to your defenses."

sentences.zh: 因賜之《六經》、《四書》、《通監》。

translations.literal: Accordingly he bestowed upon him the Six Classics, the Four Books, and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed copies of the Six Classics, the Four Books, and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 自是貢獻數至，元旦及聖節皆遣使朝賀，歲以為常。

translations.literal: From then on tribute missions came frequently; on New Year's Day and the Emperor's birthday envoys were always sent to pay court congratulations, year after year as a fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute missions arrived regularly; on New Year's Day and the emperor's birthday they sent envoys to offer congratulations, and this became their annual custom.

sentences.zh: 三年正月命使往祀其國之山川。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he ordered envoys to go and sacrifice to the mountains and rivers of their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he dispatched envoys to perform sacrifices to the mountains and rivers of their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 是歲頒科舉詔於高麗，顓表謝，貢方物，並納元所授金印。

translations.literal: That year the imperial examination edict was promulgated in Goryeo; Zhuan submitted a memorial of thanks, presented local products, and also surrendered the golden seal granted by Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the civil examination edict was issued to Goryeo; Zhuan sent a memorial of thanks, presented tribute goods, and returned the golden seal that Yuan had bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 中書省言：「高麗貢使多齎私物入貨，宜徵稅；

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "Goryeo tribute envoys often bring private goods to sell for profit; taxes should be levied;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "Goryeo tribute envoys often carry private goods to sell in the markets; they should be taxed;

sentences.zh: 又多攜中國物出境，禁之便。」

translations.literal: they also often carry Chinese goods out of the country; prohibiting this would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: and they frequently take Chinese goods out of the country; it would be prudent to forbid this."

sentences.zh: 俱不許。

translations.literal: Both were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were rejected.

sentences.zh: 五年表請遣子弟入太學，帝曰：「入學固美事，但涉海遠，不欲者勿強。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year he submitted a memorial requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy; the Emperor said: "Entering study is indeed a fine thing, but crossing the sea is far; those who do not wish it should not be forced."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he petitioned to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy; the emperor replied: "Study at court is a worthy undertaking, but the sea crossing is long and perilous—do not compel those who are unwilling."

sentences.zh: 貢使洪師範、鄭夢周等一百五十餘人來京，失風溺死者三十九人，師範與焉。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys Hong Shifan, Zheng Mengzhou, and more than 150 others came to the capital; thirty-nine perished in shipwreck from lost winds, Shifan among them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute envoys Hong Shifan, Zheng Mengzhou, and more than 150 others sailed to the capital; thirty-nine were lost at sea in a storm, Shifan among the dead.

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，遣元樞密使延安答裏往諭入貢毋數。

translations.literal: The Emperor took pity on them and sent former Privy Council Commissioner Yanandali to instruct them not to come in tribute so frequently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved with pity and sent the former Privy Council Commissioner Yanandali to tell them not to send tribute so often.

sentences.zh: 而顓復遣其門下贊成事姜仁裕來貢馬，其賀正旦使金湑等已先至，帝悉遣還。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuan again sent his Secretariat Associate Director Jiang Renyu to present tribute horses; his New Year's Day congratulatory envoys Jin Xu and others had already arrived first—the Emperor sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuan again sent his Secretariat Associate Director Jiang Renyu to present horses in tribute, while his New Year's Day envoys led by Jin Xu had already arrived; the emperor sent them all back.

sentences.zh: 謂中書省臣曰：「高麗貢獻繁數，既困敝其民，而涉海復虞覆溺。

translations.literal: He said to the Secretariat officials: "Goryeo's tribute missions are too frequent, which both exhausts its people and again risks capsizing on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He told the Secretariat officials: "Goryeo's tribute missions come too often, wearing out its people and risking their lives on the sea.

sentences.zh: 宜遵古諸侯之禮，三年一聘。

translations.literal: They should follow the ancient ritual of feudal lords—one visit every three years.
translations.idiomatic: They should follow the ancient custom of feudal lords and send envoys once every three years.

sentences.zh: 貢物惟所產，毋過侈。

translations.literal: Tribute goods should be only what they produce, not excessively lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute should consist only of local products and must not be excessive.

sentences.zh: 其明諭朕意。」

translations.literal: Clearly convey my intent to them."
translations.idiomatic: Make my wishes clearly known to them."

sentences.zh: 六年，顓遣甲兩等貢馬五十匹，道亡其二，甲兩以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zhuan sent Jialiang and others to present fifty horses in tribute; two were lost on the road, and Jialiang reported this.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhuan sent Jialiang and others to present fifty horses; two died en route, and Jialiang reported the loss.

sentences.zh: 及進，以私馬足之。

translations.literal: When presenting them, he made up the number with private horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the horses were delivered, he made up the shortfall with his own private horses.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其不誠，卻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor detested his lack of sincerity and rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, disgusted by this lack of sincerity, refused the tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年遣監門護軍周誼、鄭庇等來貢，表請每歲一貢，貢道從陸，由定遼，毋涉海，其貢物稱「送太府監」。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he sent Gate Guard Commander Zhou Yi, Zheng Bi, and others to present tribute, submitting a memorial requesting tribute once every year, with the tribute route overland through Dingliao and not crossing the sea; the tribute goods were labeled "delivered to the Imperial Storehouse Directorate."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he sent Gate Guard Commander Zhou Yi, Zheng Bi, and others with tribute, petitioning for annual missions by land through Dingliao rather than by sea, and labeling the goods as "for delivery to the Imperial Storehouse Directorate."

sentences.zh: 中書省言：「元時有太府監，本朝未嘗有，言涉不誠。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "In Yuan times there was an Imperial Storehouse Directorate, but our dynasty has never had one; the wording suggests insincerity."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "The Yuan had an Imperial Storehouse Directorate, but our dynasty has no such office—the wording suggests bad faith."

sentences.zh: 帝命卻其貢。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered their tribute rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the tribute refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲顓為權相李仁人所弑。

translations.literal: That year Zhuan was assassinated by the powerful minister Li Renren.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhuan was assassinated by the powerful minister Li Renren.

sentences.zh: 顓無子，以寵臣辛肫之子禑為子，於是仁人立禑。

translations.literal: Zhuan had no son and had adopted the son of his favored minister Xin Chun, named Biao, as his heir; thereupon Renren enthroned Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan had no son of his own and had adopted Biao, son of his favored minister Xin Chun, as heir; Renren then installed Biao on the throne.

sentences.zh: 八年，禑遣判宗簿事崔原來告哀，且言前有貢使金義殺朝使蔡斌，今嗣王禑已誅義，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Biao sent Director of the Registry of Ancestors Cui Yuan to announce mourning, and also stated that previously the tribute envoy Jin Yi had killed the Ming envoy Cai Bin, and that the succeeding king Biao had already executed Yi and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Biao sent Registry Director Cui Yuan to announce the mourning, reporting that a former tribute envoy named Jin Yi had killed the Ming envoy Cai Bin, and that the new king Biao had executed Yi and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其詐，拘原而遣使往祭吊。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected deception, detained Yuan, and sent envoys to perform sacrificial rites of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected fraud, detained Yuan, and dispatched envoys to offer sacrificial condolences.

sentences.zh: 十年，使來請故王顓諡號，帝曰：「顓被殺已久，今始請諡，將假吾朝命，鎮撫其民，且掩其弑逆之跡，不可許。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, envoys came requesting a posthumous title for the former king Zhuan; the Emperor said: "Zhuan was killed long ago, and now they first request a posthumous title—they intend to borrow our dynasty's authority to pacify their people and moreover cover up their regicidal traces; this cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year envoys came requesting a posthumous title for the late King Zhuan; the emperor said: "Zhuan was murdered long ago, and they ask for a title only now—they wish to borrow our authority to pacify their people and cover up their regicide; this cannot be granted.

sentences.zh: 前所留使者，其遣之。」

translations.literal: The envoys previously detained—send them back."
translations.idiomatic: As for the envoys we have been holding, send them back."

sentences.zh: 於是釋原歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was then released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 其夏，復遣周誼貢馬及方物，卻不受。

translations.literal: That summer, Zhou Yi was again sent to present horses and local products, but they were rejected and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Zhou Yi was again sent with horses and tribute goods, but the emperor refused them.

sentences.zh: 冬，又遣使賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In winter, envoys were again sent to congratulate the coming New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they again sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高麗王顓被弑，奸臣竊命，《春秋》之義，亂臣必誅，夫又何言。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The King of Goryeo Zhuan was assassinated, and treacherous ministers usurped authority; by the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebellious ministers must be punished—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "King Zhuan of Goryeo was murdered and treacherous ministers seized power; by the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, rebels must be punished—what more need be said?

sentences.zh: 第前後使者皆稱嗣王所遣，中書宜遣人往問嗣王如何，政令安在。

translations.literal: Only, the envoys before and after all claim to be sent by the succeeding king; the Secretariat should send someone to inquire how the succeeding king is and where government orders reside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every envoy claims to be sent by the new king; the Secretariat should dispatch someone to inquire after the new king's condition and where authority now lies.

sentences.zh: 若政令如前，嗣王不為羈囚，則當依前王言，歲貢馬千匹，明年貢金百斤、銀萬兩、良馬百、細布萬，仍悉送還所拘遼東民，方見王位真而政令行，朕無惑已。

translations.literal: If government orders are as before and the succeeding king is not a captive, then according to the former king's words they should present a thousand horses in tribute each year; next year present a hundred jin of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, a hundred fine horses, and ten thousand bolts of fine cloth, and also fully return all detained Liaodong people—only then will it be seen that the kingship is genuine and government orders are enforced, and I will have no further doubts.
translations.idiomatic: If government proceeds as before and the new king is not a prisoner, then as the late king promised they must present a thousand horses each year; next year they must also send a hundred jin of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, a hundred fine horses, and ten thousand bolts of fine cloth, and return all Liaodong subjects we hold in detention—only then will it be clear that the throne is legitimate and authority is intact, and I shall have no further doubts.

sentences.zh: 否則弑君之賊，必討無赦。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the regicide rebels must be punished without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the king-killers must be punished without mercy."

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，禑復命誼來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, Biao again ordered Yi to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Biao again sent Yi with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年敕遼東守將潘敬、葉旺等謹飭邊備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he ordered the Liaodong frontier generals Pan Jing, Ye Wang, and others to carefully maintain border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he ordered the Liaodong frontier commanders Pan Jing and Ye Wang to tighten border defenses.

sentences.zh: 其冬，禑遣李茂芳等來貢，以不如約卻之。

translations.literal: That winter, Biao sent Li Maofang and others with tribute, but they were rejected for not fulfilling the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Biao sent Li Maofang and others with tribute, but they were turned away for failing to meet the agreed terms.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遼東送高麗使誼至京師，帝敕敬等曰：「高麗弑君，又殺朝使，前堅請入貢又不如期，今遣誼來，以虛文飾詐，他日必為邊患。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Liaodong escorted the Goryeo envoy Yi to the capital; the Emperor instructed Jing and others: "Goryeo assassinated its king and also killed a Ming envoy; previously they urgently requested to send tribute yet failed to meet the deadline; now sending Yi with empty words to disguise deception—they will surely become a border threat one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Liaodong escorted the Goryeo envoy Yi to the capital; the emperor instructed Jing and the others: "Goryeo murdered its king and killed our envoy; they pleaded to send tribute yet missed the deadline; now they send Yi with empty words to mask their deceit—they will surely become a border menace.

sentences.zh: 自今來者，其絕勿通。」

translations.literal: From now on, cut off all who come and do not receive them."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, refuse all further envoys and cut off contact."

sentences.zh: 因留誼于京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was detained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was then detained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十六年來貢，卻之，命禮部責其朝貢過期、陪臣侮慢之罪；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year they came with tribute and were rejected; he ordered the Ministry of Rites to rebuke them for overdue tribute missions and the disrespect of accompanying ministers;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year they sent tribute and were refused; he ordered the Ministry of Rites to rebuke them for overdue missions and the insolence of their accompanying ministers;

sentences.zh: 誠欲聽約者，當以前五歲違約不貢之物並至。

translations.literal: if they truly wish to abide by the agreement, they should bring together all goods owed from the previous five years of broken agreements.
translations.idiomatic: if they truly wished to honor the agreement, they must deliver all tribute owed from the five years of default.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，禑遣司僕正崔涓、禮儀判書金進宜貢馬二千匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, Biao sent Director of the Stud Cui Juan and Director of Ceremonies Jin Jinyi to present two thousand horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Biao sent Stud Director Cui Juan and Ceremonies Director Jin Jinyi with two thousand horses in tribute.

sentences.zh: 且言金非地所產，願以馬代輸，餘皆如約。

translations.literal: They also stated that gold was not produced in their land and requested to substitute horses in payment; all else would be as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported that gold was not produced locally and asked to substitute horses in its place; all other terms would be honored.

sentences.zh: 遼東守將唐勝宗為之請，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Liaodong frontier general Tang Shengzhong interceded on their behalf, and the Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong commander Tang Shengzhong pleaded on their behalf, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 然請顓諡號，襲王爵，未允也。

translations.literal: However, their requests for Zhuan's posthumous title and succession to the kingship were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Their requests for Zhuan's posthumous title and for Biao's investiture as king, however, were still denied.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，貢使至。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, the tribute envoys arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year the tribute envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝諭禮臣曰：「高麗屢請約束，朕數不允，而其請不已，故索歲貢以試其誠偽，非以此為富也。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed the Rites officials: "Goryeo repeatedly requested to be bound by agreement; I several times did not grant it, yet their requests did not cease; therefore I demanded annual tribute to test their sincerity or deception—not to enrich myself thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Rites officials: "Goryeo repeatedly asked to be bound by agreement; I refused several times, yet they persisted; so I demanded annual tribute to test their sincerity—not to enrich myself.

sentences.zh: 今既聽命，宜損其貢數，令三年一朝，貢馬五十匹。

translations.literal: Now that they have obeyed, their tribute quota should be reduced—one court visit every three years, presenting fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have submitted, reduce their tribute quota to one mission every three years with fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年正旦乃貢。」

translations.literal: They should present tribute only at the New Year's Day of the twenty-first year."
translations.idiomatic: Their next tribute should come at the New Year of the twenty-first year."

sentences.zh: 七月，禑上表請襲爵，並請故王諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Biao submitted a memorial requesting succession to the title and also requesting a posthumous title for the former king.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Biao petitioned to succeed to the kingship and requested a posthumous title for the late king.

sentences.zh: 命封禑為高麗國王，賜故王顓諡恭湣。

translations.literal: He ordered Biao enfeoffed as King of Goryeo and granted the former king Zhuan the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Biao as King of Goryeo and granted the late King Zhuan the posthumous title Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月遣使貢布萬匹、馬千匹。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year envoys were sent to present ten thousand bolts of cloth and a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year they sent envoys with ten thousand bolts of cloth and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 九月，表賀，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a memorial of congratulations was submitted and local products presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they sent a congratulatory memorial and tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 其後貢獻輒逾常額，且未嘗至三年也。

translations.literal: Thereafter their tribute frequently exceeded the regular quota and never waited until three years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter their tribute regularly exceeded the prescribed quota and never waited the full three-year interval.

sentences.zh: 冬，詔遣指揮僉事高家奴以綺布市馬於高麗。

translations.literal: In winter, an edict dispatched Assistant Commander Gao Jianu to purchase horses in Goryeo with brocade and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In winter an edict dispatched Assistant Commander Gao Jianu to buy horses in Goryeo with brocade and cloth.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，高家奴還，陳高麗表辭馬直，帝敕如數償之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, Gao Jianu returned and reported that Goryeo had submitted a memorial declining payment for the horses; the Emperor ordered full payment as counted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twentieth year Gao Jianu returned and reported that Goryeo had declined payment for the horses; the emperor ordered full compensation paid.

sentences.zh: 先是，元末遼、瀋兵起，民避亂，轉徙高麗。

translations.literal: Previously, at the end of Yuan, when warfare arose in Liaoning and Shenyang, people fleeing chaos migrated to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when warfare broke out in Liaoning and Shenyang at the end of Yuan, refugees fleeing the turmoil had migrated to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 至是因市馬，帝令就索之，遂以遼、瀋流民三百餘口來歸。

translations.literal: Now on account of the horse purchase, the Emperor ordered them sought out on the spot; thus more than three hundred refugees from Liaoning and Shenyang were returned.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, taking advantage of the horse purchase, the emperor ordered them sought out, and more than three hundred Liaoning and Shenyang refugees were returned.

sentences.zh: 十二月命戶部咨高麗王：「鐵嶺北，東西之地，舊屬開元者，遼東統之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he ordered the Ministry of Revenue to inform the King of Goryeo: "North of Tieling, the lands east and west that formerly belonged to Kaiyuan shall be administered by Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he ordered the Ministry of Revenue to notify the King of Goryeo: "North of Tieling, the lands east and west that formerly belonged to Kaiyuan shall fall under Liaodong's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 鐵嶺之南，舊屬高麗者，本國統之。

translations.literal: South of Tieling, what formerly belonged to Goryeo shall be administered by your state.
translations.idiomatic: South of Tieling, what formerly belonged to Goryeo shall remain under your kingdom's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 各正疆境，毋侵越。」

translations.literal: Each should rectify its borders and not encroach."
translations.idiomatic: Each side should respect its proper borders and refrain from encroachment."

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，禑表言，鐵嶺之地實其世守，乞仍舊便。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year, Biao submitted a memorial stating that the Tieling region was in truth held by his house for generations and requesting that the former arrangement remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year Biao petitioned that the Tieling region had been held by his house for generations and asked that the former arrangement stand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高麗舊以鴨綠江為界，今飾辭鐵嶺，詐偽昭然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Goryeo formerly took the Yalu River as its border; now dressing up words about Tieling, their fraud is plainly evident.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Goryeo's traditional border was the Yalu River; this talk of Tieling is transparent deceit.

sentences.zh: 其以朕言諭之，俾安分，毋生釁端。」

translations.literal: Convey my words to them, so they keep to their place and do not create provocations."
translations.idiomatic: Convey my words to them: let them keep to their place and not provoke trouble."

sentences.zh: 八月，高麗千戶陳景來降，言：「是年四月，禑欲寇遼東，使都軍相崔瑩、李成桂繕兵西京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Goryeo chiliarch Chen Jing came to surrender and reported: "In the fourth month of that year, Biao intended to raid Liaodong and sent the Director of Military Affairs Cui Ying and Li Chenggui to drill troops in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Goryeo chiliarch Chen Jing defected and reported: "In the fourth month of that year Biao planned to raid Liaodong and sent Military Affairs Director Cui Ying and Li Chenggui to muster troops at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 成桂使陳景屯艾州，以糧不繼退師。

translations.literal: Chenggui sent Chen Jing to garrison Aizhou; because supplies did not continue, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui posted Chen Jing at Aizhou, but the army withdrew when supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 王怒，殺成桂之子。

translations.literal: The king was enraged and killed Chenggui's son.
translations.idiomatic: The king flew into a rage and executed Chenggui's son.

sentences.zh: 成桂還兵攻破王城，囚王及瑩。」

translations.literal: Chenggui turned his army back, stormed the royal city, and imprisoned the king and Ying."
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui turned his army around, stormed the capital, and imprisoned the king and Cui Ying."

sentences.zh: 景懼及，故降。

translations.literal: Jing feared he would be implicated and therefore surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be implicated, Chen Jing defected.

sentences.zh: 帝敕遼東嚴守備，仍遣人偵之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Liaodong to strictly maintain defenses and also sent men to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liaodong to tighten its defenses and sent scouts to monitor the situation.

sentences.zh: 十月，禑請遜位於其子昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Biao requested to abdicate in favor of his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Biao asked to abdicate in favor of his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「前聞其王被囚，此必成桂之謀，姑俟之以觀變。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I previously heard their king was imprisoned; this must be Chenggui's plot—let us wait for now and observe how events unfold."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I had heard their king was imprisoned; this must be Chenggui's doing—for now let us wait and see how matters develop."

sentences.zh: 二十二年，權國事昌奏乞入朝，帝不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Chang, who held state affairs, submitted a memorial requesting to come to court; the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Chang, who was administering state affairs, petitioned to come to court; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲，成桂廢昌，而立定昌國院君瑤。

translations.literal: That year, Chenggui deposed Chang and enthroned Yao, Lord of the Dingchang State Academy.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chenggui deposed Chang and installed Yao, Lord of the Dingchang State Academy, on the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year envoys were sent to report this.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year they sent envoys to announce the change.

sentences.zh: 二十四年三月詔市馬高麗。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fourth year an edict ordered horse purchases in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-fourth year an edict authorized horse purchases in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，權國事瑤進所市馬千五百匹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yao, who held state affairs, presented the fifteen hundred horses purchased.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yao, who was administering state affairs, delivered the fifteen hundred horses purchased on order.

sentences.zh: 帝曰；

translations.literal: The Emperor said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said:

sentences.zh: 「三韓君臣悖亂，二紀於茲。

translations.literal: "The rulers and ministers of the Three Han have been rebellious and disorderly for two reign-periods now.
translations.idiomatic: "The rulers and ministers of the Three Han have been in turmoil for two reign-periods now.

sentences.zh: 今王瑤嗣立，乃王氏苗裔，宜遣使勞之。」

translations.literal: Now King Yao has succeeded to the throne; he is a descendant of the Wang house and envoys should be sent to console him."
translations.idiomatic: Now King Yao has ascended the throne; as a descendant of the Wang line, envoys should be sent to congratulate him."

sentences.zh: 十二月，瑤遣其子奭朝賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yao sent his son Shi to court to congratulate the coming New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yao sent his son Shi to court to congratulate the coming New Year.

sentences.zh: 奭未歸而成桂自立，遂有其國，瑤出居原州。

translations.literal: Before Shi returned, Chenggui declared himself ruler, seized the state, and Yao went out to reside at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shi could return, Chenggui declared himself ruler and took the kingdom; Yao was sent to live at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 王氏自五代傳國數百年，至是絕。

translations.literal: The Wang house had transmitted the state for several centuries since the Five Dynasties, and with this it ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang line had held the throne for several centuries since the Five Dynasties period; with this it came to an end.

sentences.zh: 二十五年九月，高麗知密直司事趙胖等持國都評議司奏言：「本國自恭湣王薨，無嗣，權臣李仁人以辛肫子禑主國事，昏暴好殺，至欲興師犯邊，大將李成桂以為不可而回軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year, Goryeo Director of the Privy Office Zhao Pang and others presented a memorial from the State Capital Deliberative Office, stating: "Since the death of King Gongmin without heir, the powerful minister Li Renren installed Xin's son Biao to administer state affairs; he was benighted, violent, and fond of killing, even intending to raise troops and violate the border; the great general Li Chenggui deemed this impossible and turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year Goryeo Privy Office Director Zhao Pang and others presented a memorial from the State Deliberative Office reporting: "Since King Gongmin died without an heir, the powerful minister Li Renren installed Xin's son Biao to rule; he was tyrannical and bloodthirsty and even planned to invade the border, until General Li Chenggui refused and withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 禑負罪惶懼，遜位於子昌。

translations.literal: Biao, burdened with guilt and fear, abdicated in favor of his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, guilt-stricken and fearful, abdicated in favor of his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 國人弗順，啟請恭湣王妃安氏擇宗親瑤權國事。

translations.literal: The people were not compliant; they petitioned Queen Consort An of King Gongmin to select the clansman Yao to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people would not accept this and petitioned Queen Consort An of the late King Gongmin to choose the clansman Yao to administer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 已及四年，昏戾信讒，戕害勳舊，子奭癡騃不慧，國人謂瑤不足主社稷。

translations.literal: Four years had passed; he was benighted, perverse, and believed slanders, killing meritorious elders; his son Shi was dull and witless; the people said Yao was unfit to rule the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Four years had passed; Yao proved benighted and cruel, trusting slanders and killing meritorious elders; his son Shi was dull-witted, and the people judged Yao unfit to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 今以安氏命，退瑤於私第。

translations.literal: Now by Queen Consort An's command, Yao has been removed to a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: By Queen Consort An's authority, Yao has now been removed to a private residence.

sentences.zh: 王氏子姓無可當輿望者，中外人心咸系成桂。

translations.literal: Among the Wang clansmen there is none who can bear the people's hopes; within and without, all hearts turn to Chenggui.
translations.idiomatic: No member of the Wang house commands the people's trust; at court and in the country alike, all look to Chenggui.

sentences.zh: 臣等與國人耆老共推主國事，惟聖主俞允。」

translations.literal: We your ministers together with the elders of the state jointly recommend him to administer state affairs; we await the sage sovereign's gracious approval."
translations.idiomatic: We ministers together with the elders of the realm jointly recommend him to rule; we await Your Majesty's gracious approval."

sentences.zh: 帝以高麗僻處東隅，非中國所治，令禮部移諭：「果能順天道，合人心，不啟邊釁，使命往來，實爾國之福，我又何誅。」

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that Goryeo lay remote in the eastern corner and was not territory governed by the Central State, ordered the Ministry of Rites to transmit instructions: "If you can indeed follow Heaven's way, accord with the people's hearts, and not provoke border conflicts, with missions coming and going—this is truly your state's blessing; why would I punish you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering Goryeo a distant eastern realm beyond direct Chinese governance, ordered the Ministry of Rites to convey his reply: "If you truly follow Heaven's way, win the people's hearts, and refrain from provoking border trouble, with envoys coming and going freely—that will be your kingdom's blessing, and I shall have no cause to punish you."

sentences.zh: 冬，成桂聞皇太子薨，遣使表慰，並請更國號。

translations.literal: In winter, Chenggui heard that the Crown Prince had died and sent envoys with a memorial of condolence, also requesting to change the state name.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Chenggui learned of the crown prince's death and sent envoys with condolences, also requesting a change of the kingdom's name.

sentences.zh: 帝命仍古號曰朝鮮。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that the ancient name Joseon be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the ancient name Joseon be restored.

sentences.zh: 二十六年二月遣使進馬九千八百餘匹，命運糸寧絲綿布一萬九千七百餘匹酬之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year envoys were sent to present more than nine thousand eight hundred horses; he ordered more than nineteen thousand seven hundred bolts of silk, cotton cloth, and fabric sent in payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-sixth year they sent envoys with more than nine thousand eight hundred horses; the court ordered more than nineteen thousand seven hundred bolts of silk and cotton cloth sent in payment.

sentences.zh: 六月表謝，貢馬及方物，並上前恭湣王金印，請更己名曰旦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month a memorial of thanks was submitted, horses and local products were presented, and the former King Gongmin's golden seal was surrendered; he requested to change his own name to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent a memorial of thanks with horses and tribute goods, surrendered the late King Gongmin's golden seal, and asked to change his own name to Tan.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是月，遼東都指揮使司奏，朝鮮國招引女直五百餘人，潛渡鴨綠江，欲入寇。

translations.literal: That month, the Liaodong Regional Military Commission reported that Joseon had recruited more than five hundred Jurchen, secretly crossed the Yalu River, and intended to raid.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Liaodong Regional Military Commission reported that Joseon had recruited more than five hundred Jurchen, secretly crossed the Yalu River, and planned to raid the border.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使敕諭，示以禍福。

translations.literal: Envoys were then dispatched with an imperial instruction, showing the consequences of fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The court then dispatched envoys with an imperial admonition, warning of the consequences.

sentences.zh: 旦得敕，惶懼陳謝，上貢，並械送逋逃軍民三百八十餘人至遼東。

translations.literal: Tan received the instruction, fearfully submitted an apology, sent tribute, and also sent in shackles more than three hundred eighty fugitive soldiers and civilians to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan received the admonition, submitted a fearful apology and tribute, and sent more than three hundred eighty fugitive soldiers and civilians in shackles to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，旦遣子入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Tan sent his son to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Tan sent his son to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十八年遣使柳珣賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year envoy Liu Xun was sent to congratulate the coming New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year they sent the envoy Liu Xun to congratulate the coming New Year.

sentences.zh: 帝以表文語慢，詰責之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding the memorial's language disrespectful, rebuked and censured them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found the memorial's language disrespectful and rebuked them sharply.

sentences.zh: 珣言表文乃門下評理鄭道傳所撰，遂命逮道傳，釋珣歸。

translations.literal: Xun stated that the memorial had been drafted by Secretariat Reviewer Zheng Daochuan; the Emperor then ordered Daochuan arrested and released Xun to return.
translations.idiomatic: Xun reported that the memorial had been drafted by Secretariat Reviewer Zheng Daochuan; the emperor ordered Daochuan arrested and released Xun to return home.

sentences.zh: 二十九年送撰表人鄭總等三人至，雲表實總等所撰，道傳病不能行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the memorial drafters Zheng Zong and two others were sent; they said the memorial was in fact drafted by Zong and the others, and Daochuan was ill and could not travel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year they sent the memorial drafters Zheng Zong and two others, who claimed the memorial was actually their work and that Daochuan was too ill to travel.

sentences.zh: 帝以總等亂邦構釁，留不遣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, deeming Zong and the others troublemakers who stirred conflict in the state, detained them and did not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Zong and his colleagues to be troublemakers who stirred conflict in their kingdom and detained them.

sentences.zh: 三十年冬，復以表涉譏訕，拘其使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth winter, again because the memorial involved mockery and insult, their envoys were detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirtieth year their envoys were again detained because the memorial contained insulting language.

sentences.zh: 建文初，旦表陳年老，以子芳遠襲位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, Tan submitted a memorial stating his advanced age and requesting that his son Fangyuan succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign Tan petitioned that he was advanced in years and asked that his son Fangyuan succeed him.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 成祖立，遣官頒即位詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu ascended the throne, officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he dispatched officials to deliver the accession edict.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月，芳遠遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongle, Fangyuan sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yongle Fangyuan sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 四月復遣陪臣李貴齡入貢，奏芳遠父有疾，需龍腦、沈香、蘇合、香油諸物，齎布求市。

translations.literal: In the fourth month accompanying minister Li Guiling was again sent with tribute, reporting that Fangyuan's father was ill and needed dragon's brain, aloeswood, storax, and fragrant oil; he brought cloth seeking to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month accompanying minister Li Guiling was again sent with tribute, reporting that Fangyuan's father was ill and needed camphor, aloeswood, storax, and fragrant oil; he brought cloth to purchase them.

sentences.zh: 帝命太醫院賜之，還其布。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Imperial Medical Academy to grant them and returned their cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Imperial Medical Academy to bestow the items and returned their cloth.

sentences.zh: 芳遠表謝，因請冕服書藉。

translations.literal: Fangyuan submitted a memorial of thanks and requested court robes and books.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyuan sent a memorial of thanks and requested court robes and books.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其能慕中國禮，賜金印、誥命、冕服、九章、圭玉、珮玉，妃珠翠七翟冠、霞帔、金墜，及經籍彩幣表裏。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his ability to admire Chinese ritual and bestowed a golden seal, patent of investiture, court robes, nine emblems, jade scepter and pendant, the consort's pearl-and-emerald seven-pheasant crown, cloud collar, golden pendant, and classics, silk goods, and lining fabrics.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his admiration for Chinese ritual and bestowed a golden seal, patent of investiture, court robes with nine emblems, jade scepter and pendant, the queen consort's pearl-and-emerald seven-pheasant crown with cloud collar and golden pendant, along with classics, silks, and lining fabrics.

sentences.zh: 自後貢獻，歲輒四五至焉。

translations.literal: From then on tribute missions came four or five times each year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute missions arrived four or five times each year.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月詔立芳遠子禔為世子，從其請也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year an edict established Fangyuan's son Ti as heir apparent, granting his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year an edict named Fangyuan's son Ti heir apparent, as he had requested.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，貢馬三千匹至遼東，命戶部運絹布萬五千匹償之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, three thousand tribute horses arrived at Liaodong; the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to transport fifteen thousand bolts of silk and cloth in payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year three thousand tribute horses arrived at Liaodong; the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to send fifteen thousand bolts of silk and cloth in payment.

sentences.zh: 六年，世子禔來朝，賜織金文綺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Heir Apparent Ti came to court and was granted gold-woven patterned brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Heir Apparent Ti came to court and was granted gold-woven brocade.

sentences.zh: 及歸，帝親制詩賜之。

translations.literal: When he returned, the Emperor personally composed a poem and bestowed it upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the emperor personally composed a poem and bestowed it upon him.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮納女後宮，立為妃嬪者四人。

translations.literal: At that time Joseon presented women to the inner palace; four were established as consorts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Joseon presented women to the inner palace, and four were installed as consorts.

sentences.zh: 其秋，遣陪臣鄭擢來告其父旦之喪。

translations.literal: That autumn, accompanying minister Zheng Zhuo was sent to announce the mourning for his father Tan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn accompanying minister Zheng Zhuo was sent to announce the death of his father Tan.

sentences.zh: 命官弔祭，賜諡康獻。

translations.literal: Officials were ordered to perform condolence sacrifices, and the posthumous title Kangxian was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to offer condolences, and the posthumous title Kangxian was granted.

sentences.zh: 十六年奏世子禔不肖，第三子祹孝弟力學，國人所屬，請立為嗣，詔聽王所擇。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year a memorial reported that Heir Apparent Ti was unworthy; the third son Tiao was filial, fraternal, and diligent in study, whom the people of the state looked to; he requested to be established as successor; an edict permitted the king to choose as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he reported that Heir Apparent Ti was unworthy while the third son Tiao was filial, fraternal, and diligent in study and enjoyed the people's trust; he asked to name Tiao successor, and an edict left the choice to the king.

sentences.zh: 因上表謝，並陳己年老，請以祹理國事。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial of thanks and also stated his advanced age, requesting that Tiao administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a memorial of thanks, stating his advanced age and asking that Tiao administer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 命光祿少卿韓確、鴻臚丞劉泉封祹為朝鮮國王。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Han Que and Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Liu Quan were ordered to invest Tiao as King of Joseon.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Han Que of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Assistant Director Liu Quan of the Court of State Ceremonial were ordered to invest Tiao as King of Joseon.

sentences.zh: 時帝已遷北都，朝鮮益近，而事大之禮益恭，朝廷亦待以加禮，他國不敢望也。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor had already moved to the Northern Capital; Joseon was thus nearer, and its ritual deference to the great state grew ever more respectful; the court also treated it with added honor, which other states did not dare aspire to.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had moved to the Northern Capital, bringing Joseon closer; its deference to the great power grew ever more respectful, and the court treated it with special honor that no other state could match.

sentences.zh: 二十年，芳遠卒，賜諡恭定。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Fangyuan died and was granted the posthumous title Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Fangyuan died and was granted the posthumous title Gongding.

sentences.zh: 二十一年七月，祹請立嫡子珦為世子，從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year, Tiao requested to establish his eldest son Xiang as heir apparent; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year Tiao asked to name his eldest son Xiang heir apparent, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，敕祹貢馬萬匹，至是如數至，賜白金綺絹。

translations.literal: Previously, Tiao had been ordered to present ten thousand horses in tribute; now the full number arrived and white gold and silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tiao had been ordered to present ten thousand horses; now the full quota arrived and he was rewarded with white gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年三月遣中官賜白金糸寧紗，別敕進馬五千匹，資邊用。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Xuande, eunuch officials were dispatched to bestow white gold and silk gauze; a separate edict ordered the presentation of five thousand horses to supply frontier needs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Xuande eunuch officials were sent to bestow white gold and silk gauze, and a separate edict ordered five thousand horses to supply frontier needs.

sentences.zh: 九月如數至。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the full number arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the full quota arrived.

sentences.zh: 四年祹賜書：「珍禽異獸，非朕所貴，其勿獻。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year Tiao was granted a letter: "Rare birds and exotic beasts are not what I value; do not present them."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor wrote to Tiao: "Rare birds and exotic beasts are not what I value; do not present them."

sentences.zh: 後又敕祹：「金玉之器，非爾國所產，宜止之，土物效誠而已。」

translations.literal: Later he again instructed Tiao: "Gold and jade vessels are not produced in your state; you should stop presenting them—local products to show sincerity are enough."
translations.idiomatic: Later he again instructed Tiao: "Gold and jade vessels are not produced in your kingdom; cease presenting them—local products to show sincerity are enough."

sentences.zh: 八年，祹奏遣子弟詣太學或遼東學，帝不許，賜《五經》、《四書》、《性理》、《通鑒綱目》諸書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Tiao submitted a memorial requesting to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy or the Liaodong Academy; the Emperor did not permit it and bestowed the Five Classics, Four Books, Nature and Principle, and Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Tiao petitioned to send sons and younger brothers to the Imperial Academy or the Liaodong Academy; the emperor refused but bestowed the Five Classics, Four Books, Nature and Principle, and Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 正統元年三月放朝鮮婦女金黑等五十三人還其國。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhengtong, fifty-three Joseon women including Jin Hei were released and sent back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Zhengtong fifty-three Joseon women including Jin Hei were released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 金黑等自宣德初至京師，至是遣中官送回。

translations.literal: Jin Hei and the others had come to the capital from the beginning of Xuande; now eunuch officials were dispatched to escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Hei and the others had been in the capital since the beginning of Xuande; eunuch officials were now dispatched to escort them home.

sentences.zh: 三年八月賜祹遠遊冠、絳紗袍、玉佩、赤舄。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year Tiao was granted the distant-travel cap, crimson gauze robe, jade pendant, and red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year Tiao was granted the distant-travel cap, crimson gauze robe, jade pendant, and red ceremonial shoes.

sentences.zh: 先是，建州長童倉避居朝鮮界，已復還建州。

translations.literal: Previously, Jianzhou chieftain Tongcang had taken refuge within Joseon's borders and had already returned to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jianzhou chieftain Tongcang had taken refuge within Joseon's borders and had already returned to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮言：「昔以窮歸臣，臣遇之善。

translations.literal: Joseon reported: "In the past he came to submit to me in his destitution, and I treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Joseon reported: "In the past he came to me in destitution and I treated him well.

sentences.zh: 今負恩還建州李滿住所，慮其同謀擾邊。」

translations.literal: Now ungratefully he has returned to Li Manzhu's place in Jianzhou; I fear they will conspire together to disturb the border."
translations.idiomatic: Now he has ungratefully returned to Li Manzhu's camp in Jianzhou, and I fear they will conspire to raid the border."

sentences.zh: 建州長言，所部為朝鮮追殺，阻留一百七十餘家。

translations.literal: The Jianzhou chieftain reported that his followers had been pursued and killed by Joseon, with more than 170 households detained.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianzhou chieftain reported that Joseon had pursued and killed his followers and detained more than 170 households.

sentences.zh: 五年詔祹還之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered Tiao to return them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict ordered Tiao to return them.

sentences.zh: 七年五月諭祹曰：「鴨綠江一帶東甯等衛，密邇王境，中多細人逃至王國，或被國人誘脅去者，無問漢人、女直，至即解京。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year Tiao was instructed: "Along the Yalu River the Dongning Guards and others lie close to your majesty's borders; many common people flee to your kingdom, or are lured and coerced away by your people—whether Han Chinese or Jurchen, send them to the capital upon arrival."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor instructed Tiao: "Along the Yalu River the Dongning Guards and others lie close to your borders; many common people flee to your kingdom or are lured away by your subjects—whether Han Chinese or Jurchen, send them to the capital upon arrival."

sentences.zh: 初，瓦剌密令女直諸部誘朝鮮，使背中國。

translations.literal: Previously, Oirat had secretly ordered the Jurchen tribes to entice Joseon and turn it against the Central State.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Oirat had secretly ordered the Jurchen tribes to entice Joseon into turning against China.

sentences.zh: 祹拒之，白其事於朝。

translations.literal: Tiao refused and reported the matter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao refused and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠，敕獎之，並賜彩幣。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his loyalty, issued an edict commending him, and also bestowed colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty, commended him by edict, and bestowed colored silks.

sentences.zh: 九年春，倭寇犯邊，祹命將擒獲五十餘人，械送京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, when Wō raiders violated the border, Tiao ordered his generals to capture more than fifty men and send them in shackles to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year, when Japanese raiders violated the border, Tiao ordered his generals to capture more than fifty men and send them in shackles to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年又獲餘黨來獻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the remaining band was again captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the remaining bandits were again captured and presented.

sentences.zh: 帝連敕獎諭，賜賚加等。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly issued edicts of commendation and bestowed rewards of elevated rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts of commendation and bestowed enhanced rewards.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，命使調發朝鮮及野人女直兵會遼東，征北寇。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth winter, envoys were ordered to mobilize Joseon and Wild Jurchen troops to assemble in Liaodong and campaign against northern raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year envoys were ordered to mobilize Joseon and Wild Jurchen troops to assemble in Liaodong for a campaign against northern raiders.

sentences.zh: 時英宗北狩，郕王即位，遣官頒詔于其國。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign; the Prince of Cheng ascended the throne and dispatched officials to promulgate an edict in their state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yingzong had been captured on the northern campaign; the Prince of Cheng ascended the throne and dispatched officials to deliver an edict to their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年貢馬五百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, five hundred horses were presented in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai five hundred horses were presented in tribute.

sentences.zh: 奏稱奉敕辦馬二三萬匹，比因鄰寇構釁，馬畜踣斃，一時未能。

translations.literal: A memorial stated that by imperial order they were to supply twenty or thirty thousand horses, but recently because neighboring raiders provoked conflict, horses and livestock had fallen and died, and they could not do so for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial reported that by imperial order they were to supply twenty or thirty thousand horses, but neighboring raiders had recently provoked conflict and many horses and livestock had perished, so they could not fulfill the quota for the moment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寇今少息。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The raiders have now somewhat subsided.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The raiders have now subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 馬已至者，償其直。

translations.literal: For horses already arrived, pay their price.
translations.idiomatic: For horses already delivered, pay the full price.

sentences.zh: 未至者，止勿貢。」

translations.literal: For those not yet arrived, stop and do not present tribute."
translations.idiomatic: For those not yet delivered, cease and do not send further tribute."

sentences.zh: 是年夏，祹卒，賜弔祭，諡莊憲，封子珦為國王。

translations.literal: That summer, Tiao died; condolence sacrifices were bestowed, the posthumous title Zhuangxian was granted, and his son Xiang was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Tiao died; condolence sacrifices were bestowed, the posthumous title Zhuangxian was granted, and his son Xiang was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 會遼東奏報開原、瀋陽有寇入境，掠人畜，系建州、海西、野人女直頭目李滿住等為嚮導，因諭珦相為掎角截殺之。

translations.literal: At the same time Liaodong reported that raiders had entered the territory of Kaiyuan and Shenyang, plundering people and livestock; the Jianzhou, Haixi, and Wild Jurchen chieftains Li Manzhu and others were implicated as guides; Xiang was therefore instructed to coordinate pincer attacks and intercept and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Liaodong reported raiders entering Kaiyuan and Shenyang, plundering people and livestock; Jianzhou, Haixi, and Wild Jurchen chieftains including Li Manzhu were implicated as guides, and Xiang was instructed to coordinate pincer attacks to intercept and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 其秋，續貢馬千五百餘匹。

translations.literal: That autumn, an additional fifteen hundred or more horses were presented in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an additional fifteen hundred or more horses were presented in tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜冕服，並償其直。

translations.literal: Court robes were bestowed and their price paid.
translations.idiomatic: Court robes were bestowed and full payment made.

sentences.zh: 冬又賜珦及妃權氏誥命，封其子弘為世子。

translations.literal: In winter patents of investiture were again bestowed upon Xiang and his consort Lady Quan, and his son Hongye was invested as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In winter patents of investiture were again bestowed upon Xiang and his consort Lady Quan, and his son Hongye was invested as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，以建州頭目潛與朝鮮通，戒珦絕其使。

translations.literal: In the second winter, because Jianzhou chieftains were secretly in contact with Joseon, Xiang was admonished to cut off relations with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second winter, because Jianzhou chieftains were secretly in contact with Joseon, Xiang was admonished to sever relations with them.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，珦卒，來告哀。

translations.literal: In the third autumn, Xiang died and envoys came to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third autumn Xiang died and envoys came to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 遣中官往弔祭，賜諡恭順，命子弘嗣立。

translations.literal: Eunuch officials were dispatched to perform condolence sacrifices; the posthumous title Gongshun was granted, and his son Hongye was ordered to succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch officials were dispatched to offer condolences; the posthumous title Gongshun was granted, and his son Hongye was ordered to succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 弘立三年，以年幼且嬰夙疾，請以叔瑈權國事。

translations.literal: Hongye had reigned three years; because he was young and afflicted with a chronic illness from infancy, he requested that his uncle Jun administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongye had reigned three years; because he was young and afflicted with a chronic illness from infancy, he asked that his uncle Jun administer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年上表遜位，乃封瑈為國王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he submitted a memorial abdicating; Jun was then invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he petitioned to abdicate, and Jun was then invested as king.

sentences.zh: 瑈請立子暲為世子，從之。

translations.literal: Jun requested to establish his son Yang as heir apparent; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked to name his son Yang heir apparent, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，邊將奏，有建州三衛都督私與朝鮮結，恐為中國患。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, frontier generals reported that commanders of the three Jianzhou guards were privately allied with Joseon, fearing they would become a threat to the Central State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianshun frontier generals reported that commanders of the three Jianzhou guards were privately allied with Joseon, fearing they would become a threat to China.

sentences.zh: 因敕瑈毋作不靖，貽後悔。

translations.literal: Jun was therefore admonished not to act disruptively and bring later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was therefore admonished not to stir trouble and bring later regret.

sentences.zh: 瑈疏辨，復諭曰：「宣德、正統年間，以王國與彼互相侵掠，敕解怨息兵，初不令交通給賞授官也。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial in defense; he was again instructed: "During the Xuande and Zhengtong years, because your kingdom and they mutually raided each other, an edict ordered the settling of grievances and cessation of arms—it never authorized contact, bestowal of rewards, or granting of offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial in defense; he was again instructed: "During the Xuande and Zhengtong years, because your kingdom and they raided each other, an edict ordered you to settle grievances and cease hostilities—it never authorized contact, bestowal of rewards, or granting of offices.

sentences.zh: 彼既受朝廷官職，王又加之，是與朝廷抗也。

translations.literal: They have already received offices from the court, and your majesty adds to them—this is opposing the court.
translations.idiomatic: They already hold offices from the court, and you grant them offices as well—this is to set yourself against the court.

sentences.zh: 王素秉禮義，何爾文過飾非？

translations.literal: Your majesty has always upheld ritual and righteousness—why do you now use words to gloss over faults and conceal wrongs?
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty has always upheld ritual and righteousness—why do you now embellish your faults and cover up your wrongdoing?

sentences.zh: 後宜絕私交，以全令譽。」

translations.literal: Hereafter you ought to sever private associations, so as to preserve your excellent reputation."
translations.idiomatic: From now on you should cut off private ties so as to preserve your fine reputation."

sentences.zh: 四年復諭瑈曰：「王奏毛憐衛都督郎卜兒哈通謀煽亂，已置之法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jun was again instructed: "Your majesty reported that Nibolihai, commander of the Maolian Guard, had conspired to incite rebellion, and that he has already been executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Jun was again instructed: "Your majesty reported that Nibolihai, commander of the Maolian Guard, had conspired to incite rebellion and that he has already been put to death according to law.

sentences.zh: 夫法止可行于國中，豈得加於鄰境。

translations.literal: The law may be applied only within one's own state—how can it be imposed on a neighboring territory?
translations.idiomatic: The law applies only within one's own realm—how can it be imposed on a neighbor's territory?

sentences.zh: 郎卜兒哈有罪，宜奏朝廷區處。

translations.literal: If Nibolihai was guilty, you should have reported it to the court for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: If Nibolihai was guilty, you should have reported the matter to the court for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 今輒行殺害，何怪其子阿比車之思復仇也。

translations.literal: Now you have rashly carried out a killing—why should his son Abiche's desire for revenge be surprising?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have taken it upon yourself to kill him, why should his son Abiche's wish for revenge be surprising?

sentences.zh: 聞阿比車之母尚在，宜急送遼東都司，令阿比車領回，以解仇怨。」

translations.literal: I hear that Abiche's mother is still alive; you should promptly send her to the Liaodong Regional Military Commission and let Abiche take her back, so as to resolve the enmity."
translations.idiomatic: I hear Abiche's mother is still alive; you should promptly send her to the Liaodong Regional Military Commission and let Abiche take her back, so as to settle the feud."

sentences.zh: 五年，建州衛野人至義州殺掠，瑈奏乞朝命還所掠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, wild tribesmen of the Jianzhou Guard came to Yizhou to kill and plunder; Jun submitted a memorial requesting an imperial order for the return of what had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jianzhou tribesmen raided Yizhou, killing and plundering; Jun petitioned for an imperial order to have the loot returned.

sentences.zh: 兵部議：「朝鮮先嘗誘殺郎卜兒哈，繼又誘致都指揮兀克，縱兵掠其家屬。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated: "Joseon had earlier lured and killed Nibolihai, and then lured in the commander-in-chief Wuke and sent troops to plunder his family members.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War deliberated: "Joseon had earlier lured and killed Nibolihai, then enticed the commander-in-chief Wuke and sent troops to plunder his family.

sentences.zh: 今野人實系復仇，宜諭朝鮮，寇盜之來皆自取，惟守分安法，庶弭邊釁。」

translations.literal: Now the wild tribesmen are in fact seeking revenge; Joseon should be instructed that the raids it suffers are all of its own making, and that only by keeping to its proper station and observing the law can border conflicts be quelled."
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen are in fact seeking revenge; Joseon should be told that these raids are entirely of its own making, and that only by keeping to its proper place and observing the law can border trouble be averted."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 成化元年冬，陪臣李門炯來朝，卒於道。

translations.literal: In the first winter of the Chenghua reign, the attending minister Li Menjiong came to court and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first winter of Chenghua, the attending minister Li Menjiong came to court but died en route.

sentences.zh: 命給棺賜祭，並賜彩幣慰其家。

translations.literal: An order was issued to provide a coffin and grant sacrificial offerings, and colored silks were also bestowed to console his family.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a coffin and sacrificial offerings provided, and also bestowed colored silks to console his family.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮頻貢異物，三年春，敕諭瑈修常貢，勿事珍奇。

translations.literal: At that time Joseon frequently presented rare objects; in the third spring an edict instructed Jun to restore the regular tribute and not pursue curiosities.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Joseon was frequently sending rare objects as tribute; in the third spring an edict instructed Jun to restore the regular tribute and cease presenting curiosities.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷用兵征建州，敕瑈助兵進剿。

translations.literal: At that time the court was campaigning against Jianzhou and ordered Jun to assist with troops in the advance and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was campaigning against Jianzhou and ordered Jun to send troops to assist in the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 瑈遣中樞府知事康純統眾萬餘渡鴨綠、潑豬二江，攻破九獮府諸寨，斬獲多。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched Kang Chun, director of the Central Secretariat Office, to lead more than ten thousand men across the Yalu and Poju Rivers, storm the stockades of Jiuxian Prefecture, and achieve many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Jun dispatched Kang Chun, director of the Central Secretariat Office, to lead more than ten thousand men across the Yalu and Poju Rivers, storm the stockades of Jiuxian Prefecture, and take many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 四年正月遣官來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year officials were dispatched to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year officials were sent to present captives.

sentences.zh: 詔從厚賚，敕獎諭之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered generous rewards, and an instruction of commendation was issued.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered generous rewards, and a commendatory instruction was issued.

sentences.zh: 是年，瑈卒，賜諡惠莊。

translations.literal: That year Jun died and was granted the posthumous title Huizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jun died and was granted the posthumous title Huizhuang.

sentences.zh: 遣太監鄭同、崔安封世子晄為王，給妃韓氏誥命。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Zheng Tong and Cui An were dispatched to invest the heir apparent Hwan as king and to grant a patent of investiture to his consort Lady Han.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Zheng Tong and Cui An were dispatched to invest the heir apparent Hwan as king and to grant a patent of investiture to his consort Lady Han.

sentences.zh: 既行，巡按遼東御史侯英奏曰：「遼東連年被寇，瘡痍未起，今復禾稼不登，軍民乏食。

translations.literal: After they had set out, the Liaodong touring censor Hou Ying submitted a memorial, saying: "Liaodong has been raided year after year; its wounds have not yet healed, and now the harvests have again failed, leaving soldiers and civilians short of food.
translations.idiomatic: After they had set out, the Liaodong touring censor Hou Ying submitted a memorial, saying: "Liaodong has been raided year after year; its wounds have not yet healed, and now the harvests have again failed, leaving soldiers and civilians without enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 太監鄭同等隨從人員所過驛騷。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zheng Tong and his accompanying personnel have caused disturbances at every relay station they have passed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zheng Tong and his entourage have caused disturbances at every relay station they have passed.

sentences.zh: 臣考先年曾于翰林院中，選有學行文望者出使。

translations.literal: Your subject finds that in earlier years men of learning, literary accomplishment, and reputation were selected from the Hanlin Academy to serve as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject finds that in earlier years men of learning, literary accomplishment, and reputation were selected from the Hanlin Academy to serve as envoys.

sentences.zh: 今同、安俱朝鮮人，墳墓宗族皆在，見其國王，不免屈節，殊褻中國體。

translations.literal: Now Tong and An are both men of Joseon; their ancestral graves and clans are all there, and in audience with their king they must demean themselves—this greatly debases the dignity of the Central State.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tong and An are both men of Joseon; their ancestral graves and clans are all there, and in audience with their king they must demean themselves—this greatly debases the dignity of China.

sentences.zh: 乞寢成命，或翰林，或給事中及行人內推選一員，往使為便。」

translations.literal: I beg that the existing order be suspended, and that one man be chosen from among the Hanlin Academy, the supervising secretaries, or the courier officials to go as envoy instead."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the existing order be suspended and that one man be chosen from among the Hanlin Academy, the supervising secretaries, or the courier officials to serve as envoy instead."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「英所言良是。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What Ying has said is entirely correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What Ying has said is entirely correct.

sentences.zh: 自後賞賚遣內臣，其冊封正副使，選廷臣有學行者。」

translations.literal: Henceforth rewards and gifts may be sent by inner court officials, but for the chief and deputy investiture envoys, court officials of learning and conduct shall be selected."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth rewards and gifts may be sent by inner-court officials, but the chief and deputy investiture envoys shall be chosen from among learned and upright court officials."

sentences.zh: 六年，晄病篤，以所生子幼，命其兄故世子暲女子娎子權國事，遣陪臣以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hwan was gravely ill; because the son he had fathered was young, he appointed Yeol, son of his elder brother the former heir apparent Yang, to administer state affairs, and dispatched attending ministers to report this.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hwan fell gravely ill; because his own son was still young, he appointed Yeol, son of his elder brother the former heir apparent Yang, to administer state affairs, and sent attending ministers to report the matter.

sentences.zh: 及卒，賜諡襄悼，命娎嗣位，娎妻韓氏封王妃。

translations.literal: When he died, the posthumous title Xiangdao was granted; Yeol was ordered to succeed to the throne, and Yeol's wife Lady Han was enfeoffed as queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the posthumous title Xiangdao was granted; Yeol was ordered to succeed to the throne, and Yeol's wife Lady Han was enfeoffed as queen consort.

sentences.zh: 十年追贈娎父世子暲為國王，諡懷簡，母韓氏為王妃，從所請也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yeol's father, the heir apparent Yang, was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Huaijian, and his mother Lady Han as queen consort, in accordance with the request.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Yeol's father, the heir apparent Yang, was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Huaijian, and his mother Lady Han as queen consort, as requested.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，娎奏建州野人糾聚毛憐等衛侵擾邊境不已，乞朝命戒飭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Yeol submitted a memorial that Jianzhou wild tribesmen had gathered with the Maolian and other guards to harass the border without cease, and requested an imperial order of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Yeol reported that Jianzhou tribesmen had gathered with the Maolian and other guards to harass the border without cease, and requested an imperial order of admonition.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，娎為繼妻尹氏請封，賜誥命冠服。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year Yeol requested investiture for his second wife Lady Yin, and patents of investiture, caps, and robes were bestowed.
