translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year Yeol requested investiture for his second wife Lady Yin, and patents of investiture together with caps and robes were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 時禁外國互市兵器，娎奏：「小邦北連野人，南鄰倭島，五兵之用，不可缺一。

translations.literal: At that time foreign states were forbidden to trade in weapons; Yeol submitted a memorial: "Our small state borders wild tribes to the north and lies adjacent to the Wokou islands to the south; in the use of the five weapons, not one may be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: At that time foreign states were forbidden to trade in weapons; Yeol submitted a memorial: "Our small kingdom borders wild tribes to the north and lies adjacent to the Wokou islands to the south; in the use of the five weapons, not one may be lacking.

sentences.zh: 而弓材所需牛角，仰于上國。

translations.literal: Yet the ox horns needed for bow materials depend upon the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ox horns needed for bow materials must be obtained from the superior state.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝時嘗賜火藥、火砲，今望特許收買弓角，不與外番同禁。」

translations.literal: In the time of the August Emperor gunpowder and cannon were once granted; we now hope to be specially permitted to purchase bow horns and not be subject to the same prohibition as other foreign peoples."
translations.idiomatic: In the time of the August Emperor gunpowder and cannon were once granted; we now hope to be specially permitted to purchase bow horns and not be subject to the same prohibition as other foreign peoples."

sentences.zh: 兵部議歲市弓角五十，後以不足於用，請無限額，詔許倍市。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated on an annual purchase of fifty bow horns; later, because this was insufficient for use, a request was made for no fixed quota, and an edict permitted double the purchase.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War set an annual purchase of fifty bow horns; later, because this proved insufficient, a request was made to remove the quota, and an edict permitted double the purchase.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月命娎出兵夾擊建州女直。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Yeol was ordered to dispatch troops for a pincer attack on the Jianzhou Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Yeol was ordered to dispatch troops for a pincer attack on the Jianzhou Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 娎遂遣右贊成魚有沼率兵至滿浦江，以水泮後期。

translations.literal: Yeol then dispatched the Right Assistant Minister Yu Yuzhao to lead troops to the Manpu River, but they arrived late because the ice had melted.
translations.idiomatic: Yeol then dispatched the Right Assistant Minister Yu Yuzhao to lead troops to the Manpu River, but they arrived late because the ice had melted.

sentences.zh: 復遣左議政尹弼商、節度使金嶠等渡江進剿。

translations.literal: He then dispatched the Left State Councillor Yun Pisaang, the military commissioner Jin Qiao, and others to cross the river and advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched the Left State Councillor Yun Pisaang, the military commissioner Jin Qiao, and others to cross the river and advance in suppression.

sentences.zh: 十六年春遣陪臣來獻捷，帝命內官齎敕獎其能繼先烈，賜金幣，領兵官賞賚如例。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year attending ministers were dispatched to present a victory report; the Emperor ordered an inner-court official to carry an edict commending their ability to follow the achievements of their forebears, and gold and silks were bestowed; the officers who had led the troops received rewards according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year attending ministers were sent to report victory; the emperor ordered an inner-court official to carry an edict commending their ability to follow the achievements of their forebears, and gold and silks were bestowed; the officers who had led the troops received rewards according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 後使還，遣其臣許熙伴送。

translations.literal: When the envoys later returned, his minister Xu Xi was dispatched to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys later returned, his minister Xu Xi was dispatched to escort them.

sentences.zh: 熙歸至開州，建州騎二千邀之，掠其從卒三十余人，馬二百三十餘匹，他所亡物稱是。

translations.literal: When Xi returned to Kaizhou, two thousand Jianzhou horsemen intercepted him, seizing more than thirty of his attendants and more than 230 horses, with other losses in similar proportion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi returned to Kaizhou, two thousand Jianzhou horsemen intercepted him, seizing more than thirty of his attendants and more than 230 horses, with other losses in similar proportion.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，英國公張懋、吏部尚書尹旻等以遼東連年用兵，未可輕動，宜以此意諭娎。

translations.literal: When this was reported, the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of Personnel Yin Min, and others held that Liaodong had been at war for years and should not be lightly stirred; Yeol should be instructed to this effect.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of Personnel Yin Min, and others held that Liaodong had been at war for years and should not be lightly stirred; Yeol should be instructed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 敕遼東守臣整飭邊備，更令譯者窮究所掠，期在必得，仍賜熙白金彩幣慰安之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Liaodong frontier officials to put the border defenses in order and further commanded the interpreters to pursue the seized goods to the end, with recovery expected without fail; Xi was also granted white gold and colored silks as consolation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Liaodong frontier officials to put the border defenses in order and further commanded the interpreters to pursue the seized goods to the end, with recovery expected without fail; Xi was also granted white gold and colored silks as consolation.

sentences.zh: 十七年，娎奏繼妃尹氏失德，廢置，乞更封副室尹氏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yeol submitted a memorial that his second consort Lady Yin had lost virtue and had been deposed, and requested that his secondary consort Lady Yin be newly enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yeol reported that his second consort Lady Yin had lost virtue and had been deposed, and requested that his secondary consort Lady Yin be newly enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月封娎長子㦕為世子。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Yeol's eldest son Jeong was invested as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Yeol's eldest son Jeong was invested as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年十二月，娎卒，賜諡康靖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Hongzhi Yeol died and was granted the posthumous title Kangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Hongzhi Yeol died and was granted the posthumous title Kangjing.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，封㦕為國，妻慎氏為王妃。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year Jeong was invested as king, and his wife Lady Shen was enfeoffed as queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year Jeong was invested as king, and his wife Lady Shen was enfeoffed as queen consort.

sentences.zh: 十二年，㦕奏：「本國人屢有違禁匿海島，誘引軍民，漸至滋蔓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jeong submitted a memorial: "Our countrymen have repeatedly violated prohibitions by hiding on sea islands and enticing soldiers and civilians; this has gradually spread.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Jeong submitted a memorial: "Our countrymen have repeatedly violated prohibitions by hiding on sea islands and enticing soldiers and civilians; the problem has gradually spread.

sentences.zh: 乞許本國自行搜刷。

translations.literal: We beg permission for our state to conduct searches and purges on its own.
translations.idiomatic: We beg permission for our kingdom to conduct searches and purges on its own.

sentences.zh: 其系上國地方，請敕官追捕。」

translations.literal: As for those who fall within the territory of the superior state, we request that officials be ordered to pursue and capture them."
translations.idiomatic: As for those who fall within the territory of the superior state, we request that officials be ordered to pursue and capture them."

sentences.zh: 時遼東守臣亦奏如㦕言，報可。

translations.literal: At that time the Liaodong frontier officials also submitted a memorial agreeing with Jeong's words, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liaodong frontier officials also submitted a memorial agreeing with Jeong's report, and approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，封㦕長子為世子。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year Jeong's eldest son was invested as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Jeong's eldest son was invested as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，㦕以世子夭亡，哀慟成疾，奏請以國事付其弟懌，其國人復奏請封懌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, because the heir apparent had died young, Jeong grieved himself into illness and submitted a memorial requesting that state affairs be entrusted to his younger brother Yeok; his countrymen again submitted a memorial requesting that Yeok be invested.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, because the heir apparent had died young, Jeong grieved himself into illness and petitioned to entrust state affairs to his younger brother Yeok; his subjects again petitioned to invest Yeok.

sentences.zh: 禮部議命懌權理國事，俟㦕卒乃封。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites deliberated and ordered Yeok to administer state affairs provisionally, with investiture to follow only after Jeong's death.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites ordered Yeok to administer state affairs provisionally, with investiture to follow only after Jeong's death.

sentences.zh: 既，陪臣盧公弼等以朝貢至京，復請封懌，廷議不允。

translations.literal: Later, when the attending ministers Lu Gongbi and others arrived at the capital on tribute mission, they again requested investiture for Yeok, but court deliberation did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the attending ministers Lu Gongbi and others arrived at the capital on a tribute mission, they again requested investiture for Yeok, but the court did not approve.

sentences.zh: 十二月，㦕母妃奏懌長且賢，堪付重寄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jeong's queen mother submitted a memorial that Yeok was the elder and virtuous and capable of bearing heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jeong's queen mother submitted a memorial that Yeok was the elder, virtuous, and capable of bearing heavy responsibility.

sentences.zh: 於是禮部奏：「㦕以痼疾辭位，懌以親弟承托，接受既明，友愛不失。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial: "Jeong has abdicated because of chronic illness; Yeok, as his younger brother by blood, has accepted the charge—the succession is clear and brotherly affection has not been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial: "Jeong has abdicated because of chronic illness; Yeok, as his younger brother by blood, has accepted the charge—the succession is clear and brotherly affection has not been lost.

sentences.zh: 通國臣民舉無異詞，宜順其請。」

translations.literal: Throughout the state officials and people unanimously raise no objection; their request should be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the kingdom officials and people unanimously raise no objection; their request should be granted."

sentences.zh: 上乃允懌嗣位，遣中官敕封，並賜其妃尹氏誥命。

translations.literal: The Emperor then approved Yeok's succession to the throne, dispatched an inner-court official with an edict of investiture, and also bestowed a patent of investiture upon his consort Lady Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then approved Yeok's succession to the throne, dispatched an inner-court official with an edict of investiture, and also bestowed a patent of investiture upon his consort Lady Yin.

sentences.zh: 初，成桂之自立也，與宰相李仁人本異族。

translations.literal: Initially, when Chenggui established himself in power, he and the chief minister Li Renren were of different clans.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Chenggui established himself in power, he and the chief minister Li Renren were of different clans.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，降祭海岳祝文，稱成桂為仁人子，而《祖訓》亦載仁人子成桂更名旦。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, when sacrificial texts for the seas and mountains were issued, Chenggui was called a son of Renren, and the Ancestral Admonitions also recorded that Chenggui, son of Renren, changed his name to Dan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, when sacrificial texts for the seas and mountains were issued, Chenggui was called a son of Renren, and the Ancestral Admonitions also recorded that Chenggui, son of Renren, changed his name to Dan.

sentences.zh: 後成桂子芳遠奏辨，太宗許令改正。

translations.literal: Later Chenggui's son Fangyuan submitted a memorial in defense, and the Taizong Emperor permitted the correction.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chenggui's son Fangyuan submitted a memorial in defense, and the Taizong Emperor permitted the correction.

sentences.zh: 至是修《大明會典》，仍列《祖訓》于朝鮮國。

translations.literal: At this time, when the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming was being revised, the Ancestral Admonitions was still listed under the Joseon state.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, when the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming was being revised, the Ancestral Admonitions was still listed under Joseon.

sentences.zh: 貢使市以歸，懌上疏備陳世系，辨先世無弑逆事，乞改正。

translations.literal: The tribute envoys purchased copies and returned home; Yeok submitted a memorial fully setting forth the royal lineage, arguing that no regicide or rebellion had occurred in earlier generations, and requesting correction.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute envoys purchased copies and returned home; Yeok submitted a memorial fully setting forth the royal lineage, arguing that no regicide or rebellion had occurred in earlier generations, and requesting correction.

sentences.zh: 禮部議：「《會典》詳載本朝制度，事涉外國，疑似之際，在所略。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites deliberated: "The Collected Statutes records in detail the institutions of this dynasty; matters involving foreign states, when doubtful, are appropriately omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites deliberated: "The Collected Statutes records in detail the institutions of this dynasty; matters involving foreign states, when doubtful, are appropriately omitted.

sentences.zh: 況成桂得國出皇祖命，其不系仁人後，太宗詔可征，宜從其請。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Chenggui's acquisition of the state issued from the command of the imperial ancestor; that he was not descended from Renren is attested by the Taizong Emperor's edict of approval—his request should be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Chenggui's acquisition of the throne issued from the command of the imperial ancestor; that he was not descended from Renren is attested by the Taizong Emperor's edict of approval—his request should be granted."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，命內官封懌子峼為世子，賜懌金帛珠玉，令括取異物及童男女以進。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year an inner-court official was ordered to invest Yeok's son Geo as heir apparent; Yeok was granted gold, silks, pearls, and jade, and ordered to gather rare objects and boys and girls to present as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year an inner-court official was ordered to invest Yeok's son Geo as heir apparent; Yeok was granted gold, silks, pearls, and jade, and ordered to gather rare objects and boys and girls to present as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十六年，世宗即位，禮官言：「天子初踐祚，宜正中國之體，絕外裔狎侮之端。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Shizong ascended the throne; the ritual officials said: "When the Son of Heaven has just taken the throne, the dignity of the Central State should be upheld and the beginnings of familiarity and contempt from foreign peoples cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Shizong ascended the throne; the ritual officials said: "When the Son of Heaven has just taken the throne, the dignity of China should be upheld and the beginnings of familiarity and contempt from foreign peoples cut off.

sentences.zh: 請諭懌非朝廷意，召內臣還，毋有所索取。」

translations.literal: We request that Yeok be instructed that this was not the court's intent, that the inner-court officials be recalled, and that nothing be demanded."
translations.idiomatic: We request that Yeok be told this was not the court's intent, that the inner-court officials be recalled, and that nothing be demanded."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年八月，以俘獲倭夷來獻，並送還中國被掠八人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Jiajing captives of Wokou were presented as tribute, and eight persons from China who had been seized were also sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Jiajing captives of Wokou were presented as tribute, and eight persons from China who had been seized were also sent back.

sentences.zh: 賜白金錦糸寧。

translations.literal: White gold, brocade, and cotton were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: White gold, brocade, and cotton were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 八年八月，陪臣柳溥上言：國祖李旦系本國全州人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year the attending minister Liu Pu submitted a statement: the dynastic founder Li Dan was a native of Jeonju in our state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eighth year the attending minister Liu Pu submitted a statement: the dynastic founder Li Dan was a native of Jeonju in our kingdom.

sentences.zh: 二十八世祖瀚仕新羅為司空。

translations.literal: His twenty-eighth-generation ancestor Han served Silla as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His twenty-eighth-generation ancestor Han served Silla as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 新羅亡，六世孫兢休入高麗。

translations.literal: When Silla perished, the sixth-generation descendant Jingxiu entered Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: When Silla perished, the sixth-generation descendant Jingxiu entered Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十三世孫安社仕元為南京千戶所達魯花赤。

translations.literal: The thirteenth-generation descendant Anshe served the Yuan as darughachi of the Nanjing chiliarch office.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth-generation descendant Anshe served the Yuan as darughachi of the Nanjing chiliarch office.

sentences.zh: 元季兵興，安曾孫子春與男成桂避地東遷。

translations.literal: When warfare arose in the late Yuan, An's great-great-grandson Zichun and his son Chenggui moved eastward to escape the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare arose in the late Yuan, An's great-great-grandson Zichun and his son Chenggui moved eastward to escape the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 至正辛丑，當恭湣王之十年，有紅巾賊入境，成桂擊賊有功，授武班職事，時尚未知名。

translations.literal: In the xinchou year of Zhizheng, the tenth year of King Gongmin, Red Turban bandits entered the territory; Chenggui fought the bandits with merit and was appointed to a military office, though he was not yet well known.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year of Zhizheng, the tenth year of King Gongmin, Red Turban bandits entered the territory; Chenggui fought the bandits with merit and was appointed to a military office, though he was not yet well known.

sentences.zh: 恭湣無嗣，陰蓄寵臣辛肫之子禑為子，晚為嬖臣洪倫、內豎崔萬生所弑。

translations.literal: Gongmin had no heir and secretly kept Sinchun's son Biao as his own; in his later years he was murdered by the favorite minister Hong Lun and the palace attendant Cui Wansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gongmin had no heir and secretly kept Sinchun's son Biao as his own; in his later years he was murdered by the favorite minister Hong Lun and the palace attendant Cui Wansheng.

sentences.zh: 權臣李仁人誅倫、萬生而立禑，擢成桂為門下侍中。

translations.literal: The powerful minister Li Renren executed Lun and Wansheng and enthroned Biao, promoting Chenggui to Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful minister Li Renren executed Lun and Wansheng and enthroned Biao, promoting Chenggui to Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 禑遣成桂侵遼東，成桂不從，返兵。

translations.literal: Biao dispatched Chenggui to invade Liaodong; Chenggui refused and turned his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Biao dispatched Chenggui to invade Liaodong; Chenggui refused and turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 禑懼，遜位於子昌。

translations.literal: Biao was afraid and abdicated in favor of his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was afraid and abdicated in favor of his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌以偽姓見黜，復立王氏裔定昌君瑤，竄仁人於外。

translations.literal: Chang was dismissed for using a false surname; Yao, Lord of Dingchang and a descendant of the Wang house, was again enthroned, and Renren was banished abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was dismissed for using a false surname; Yao, Lord of Dingchang and a descendant of the Wang house, was again enthroned, and Renren was banished abroad.

sentences.zh: 瑤復不道，國人戴成桂，請于高皇帝，立為王，更名旦，贍瑤別邸，終其身，實未嘗為弑。

translations.literal: Yao again behaved without the Way; the people supported Chenggui, petitioned the August Emperor, and had him established as king with his name changed to Dan; Yao was provided a separate residence for the rest of his life—in fact no murder had ever occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Yao again behaved without the Way; the people supported Chenggui, petitioned the August Emperor, and had him established as king with his name changed to Dan; Yao was provided a separate residence for the rest of his life—in fact no murder had ever occurred.

sentences.zh: 前永樂、正德間屢經奏請，俱蒙俞允，而迄未改正。

translations.literal: Previously, during the Yongle and Zhengde reigns, repeated memorials had all received imperial approval, yet the record had still not been corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, during the Yongle and Zhengde reigns, repeated memorials had all received imperial approval, yet the record had still not been corrected.

sentences.zh: 今遇重修《會典》，乞賜昭雪。」

translations.literal: Now, upon the occasion of revising the Collected Statutes, we beg that this be cleared and vindicated."
translations.idiomatic: Now, upon the occasion of revising the Collected Statutes, we beg that this be cleared and vindicated."

sentences.zh: 詔送史館編纂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent to the Historiography Institute for compilation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it sent to the Historiography Institute for compilation.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，睿宗祔太廟，配享明堂禮成，懌表賀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year, when the rites were completed for installing Ruizong in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and for his associated sacrifice in the Bright Hall, Yeok submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighteenth year, when the rites were completed for installing Ruizong in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and for his associated sacrifice in the Bright Hall, Yeok submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝特禦奉天門引見，賜宴禮部。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally received them at the Gate of Receiving Heaven and granted a banquet at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally received them at the Gate of Receiving Heaven and granted a banquet at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十三年冬，懌卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-third year Yeok died.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-third year Yeok died.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月來訃，賜諡恭僖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year word of his death arrived; the posthumous title Gongxi was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year word of his death arrived; the posthumous title Gongxi was granted.

sentences.zh: 詔立其子峼。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Geo established in succession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his son Geo established in succession.

sentences.zh: 峼未逾年卒，賜諡榮靖。

translations.literal: Geo died before a year had passed and was granted the posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Geo died before a year had passed and was granted the posthumous title Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 九月，峼弟權國事峘遣使謝祭諡，並請襲封，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Geo's younger brother Hon, who was administering state affairs, dispatched envoys to thank the court for the sacrificial offerings and posthumous title and to request succession to the enfeoffment; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Geo's younger brother Hon, who was administering state affairs, dispatched envoys to thank the court for the sacrificial offerings and posthumous title and to request succession to the enfeoffment; an edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，峘遣使送下海番人六百余至邊，賜金幣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Hon dispatched envoys to send more than six hundred coastal foreigners who had gone to sea to the border, and gold and silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Hon dispatched envoys to send more than six hundred coastal foreigners who had gone to sea to the border, and gold and silks were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 二十六年正月，峘咨稱：「福建人從無泛海至本國者，因往日本市易，為風所漂，前後共獲千人以上，皆挾軍器貨物，致中國火砲亦為倭有，恐起兵端。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-sixth year Hon reported: "Never before had people from Fujian sailed the open sea to our state; going to Japan to trade, they were driven by wind and drifted ashore, and in all more than a thousand were captured before and after, all carrying weapons and goods, so that even Chinese cannon fell into Wokou hands—we fear this may provoke hostilities."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-sixth year Hon reported: "Never before had people from Fujian sailed the open sea to our kingdom; going to Japan to trade, they were driven by wind and drifted ashore, and in all more than a thousand were captured before and after, all carrying weapons and goods, so that even Chinese cannon fell into Wokou hands—we fear this may provoke hostilities."

sentences.zh: 詔：「頃年沿海奸民犯禁，福建尤甚，往往為外國所獲，有傷國體。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In recent years lawbreaking people along the coast, especially in Fujian, have repeatedly been captured by foreign states, to the injury of the state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "In recent years lawbreaking people along the coast, especially in Fujian, have repeatedly been captured by foreign states, to the injury of the state's dignity.

sentences.zh: 海道官員令巡按御史察參。

translations.literal: Maritime officials were ordered to be inspected and impeached by touring censor-investigators.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime officials were ordered to be inspected and impeached by touring censor-investigators.

sentences.zh: 仍賜王銀幣，以旌其忠。」

translations.literal: Silver and silks were still granted to the king, to commend his loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Silver and silks were still granted to the king, to reward his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 三十一年冬，以洪武、永樂間所賜樂器敝壞，奏求律管，更乞遣樂官赴京校習，許之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirty-first year, because the musical instruments bestowed during the Hongwu and Yongle reigns had worn out, a memorial requested pitch pipes and further asked that music officials be sent to the capital for instruction; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirty-first year, because the musical instruments granted during the Hongwu and Yongle reigns had fallen into disrepair, Hon petitioned for pitch pipes and asked that music officials be sent to the capital for training; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三十五年五月有倭船四自浙、直敗還，漂入朝鮮境。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirty-fifth year four Wokou ships, defeated while returning from Zhejiang and Zhili, drifted into Korean territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirty-fifth year four Japanese pirate ships, routed while retreating from Zhejiang and the Nanjing region, drifted ashore in Korea.

sentences.zh: 峘遣兵擊殲之，得中國被俘及助逆者三十餘人來獻，因賀冬至節，帝賜璽書褒諭。

translations.literal: Hon dispatched troops to attack and destroy them, captured more than thirty persons from China who had been taken prisoner and who had aided the rebels, and presented them; because of congratulations on the Winter Solstice festival, the Emperor bestowed an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Hon sent troops to attack and annihilate them, captured more than thirty Chinese prisoners and collaborators, and presented them to the court; on the occasion of the Winter Solstice tribute, the emperor granted an imperial letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 三十八年十一月奏：「今年五月，有倭寇駕船二十五隻來抵海岸，臣命將李鐸等剿殺殆盡，獲中國民陳春等三百餘人，內招通倭嚮導陳得等十六人，俱獻闕下。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirty-eighth year he submitted a memorial: "In the fifth month of this year twenty-five Wokou ships came to the coast; your subject ordered the generals Li Duo and others to exterminate them nearly to the last man, capturing more than three hundred Chinese subjects such as Chen Chun; among them were sixteen who had colluded with the Wokou and served as guides, such as Chen De—all have been presented at the court."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirty-eighth year he submitted a memorial: "In the fifth month of this year twenty-five pirate ships reached our coast; I ordered Generals Li Duo and others to destroy them almost to a man, capturing more than three hundred Chinese subjects including Chen Chun; among them were sixteen who had colluded with the pirates and served as guides, including Chen De—all have been sent to Your Majesty's court."

sentences.zh: 復降敕獎勵，厚賚銀幣，並賜鐸等有差。

translations.literal: An edict was again issued to reward him, with generous grants of silver and silks, and Li Duo and others were also bestowed upon in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of commendation was issued again, with generous gifts of silver and silks, and Li Duo and the others were rewarded according to rank.

sentences.zh: 四十二年九月，峘復上書辨先世非李仁人後，今修《會典》雖蒙厘正，乞著始祖旦、父子春之名，帝令附錄《會典》。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-second year Hon again submitted a memorial clarifying that his forebears were not descendants of Li Renren; although the newly compiled Collected Statutes had already been corrected on this point, he begged that the names of the founding ancestor Dan and his son Jachun be recorded; the Emperor ordered them appended to the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-second year Hon again petitioned to clarify that his ancestors were not descendants of Li Renren; although the revised Collected Statutes had already set the record straight, he asked that the names of the founding ancestor Dan and his son Jachun be entered; the emperor ordered them appended to the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年六月遣官頒即位詔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Longqing officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Longqing officials were dispatched to promulgate the accession edict.

sentences.zh: 時帝將幸太學，來使乞留觀禮，許之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was about to visit the Imperial Academy; the envoys requested to remain and observe the ceremony, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was about to visit the Imperial Academy; the envoys asked to stay and observe the ceremony, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，峘卒，賜諡恭憲，命其侄昖襲封。

translations.literal: That winter Hon died; the posthumous title Gongxian was granted, and his nephew Son was ordered to succeed to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hon died; he was granted the posthumous title Gongxian, and his nephew Son was ordered to succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年正月上穆宗尊諡、兩宮徽號禮成，昖表賀，獻方物馬匹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Wanli, when the rites were completed for bestowing the posthumous title upon Muzong and the honorific titles upon the two palaces, Son submitted a congratulatory memorial and presented local products and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Wanli, when the rites were completed for bestowing the posthumous title upon Emperor Muzong and the honorific titles upon the empress dowagers, Son sent a congratulatory memorial and presented tribute goods and horses.

sentences.zh: 時昖屢請賜《皇明會典》，為其先康獻王旦雪冤。

translations.literal: At that time Son repeatedly requested that the Collected Statutes of the August Ming be granted, to clear the name of his forebear King Kangxian Dan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Son repeatedly petitioned for a copy of the Collected Statutes of the August Ming, seeking to vindicate his ancestor King Kangxian Dan.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，《會典》成，適貢使愈泓在京，請給前書，以終前命。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year the Collected Statutes were completed; it happened that the tribute envoy Yu Hong was in the capital and requested the book previously promised, to fulfill the earlier command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year the Collected Statutes were completed; the tribute envoy Yu Hong happened to be in the capital and requested the promised volumes, to fulfill the earlier imperial command.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十七年十一月，陪臣奇芩等入賀冬至，奏稱本年六月，大琉球國船遭風至海岸，所有男婦合解京，給文放歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventeenth year the attending ministers Qi Qin and others came to congratulate on the Winter Solstice and reported that in the sixth month of that year a ship from Great Ryukyu had been driven by wind to the coast; all the men and women aboard should be sent together to the capital and then released with documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventeenth year the attending ministers Qi Qin and others came to offer Winter Solstice congratulations and reported that in the sixth month a ship from Great Ryukyu had been blown ashore; they asked that all the men and women aboard be sent to the capital and then released with travel documents.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十九年十一月奏，倭酋關白平秀吉聲言明年三月來犯，詔兵部申飭海防。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the nineteenth year a memorial reported that the Wokou chieftain Kampaku Hideyoshi declared he would invade in the third month of the coming year; an edict ordered the Ministry of War to tighten coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the nineteenth year a memorial reported that the Japanese warlord Kampaku Hideyoshi had declared he would invade in the third month of the coming year; an edict ordered the Ministry of War to strengthen coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 平秀吉者，薩摩州人，初隨倭關白信長。

translations.literal: Hideyoshi was a man of Satsuma province who at first followed the Wokou kampaku Nobunaga.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi was a man of Satsuma Province who had first served under the Japanese regent Nobunaga.

sentences.zh: 會信長為其下所弑，秀吉遂統信長兵，自號關白，劫降六十餘州。

translations.literal: When Nobunaga was assassinated by his subordinates, Hideyoshi thereupon took command of Nobunaga's armies, styled himself kampaku, and coerced the submission of more than sixty provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Nobunaga was murdered by his own followers, Hideyoshi seized command of Nobunaga's armies, proclaimed himself regent, and forced more than sixty provinces to submit.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮與日本對馬島相望，時有倭夷往來互市。

translations.literal: Korea and Japan's Tsushima Island face each other across the sea, and Wokou at times came and went to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Korea and Japan's Tsushima Island lay within sight of each other, and Japanese traders regularly crossed back and forth to exchange goods.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏五月，秀吉遂分渠帥行長、清正等率舟師逼釜山鎮，潛渡臨津。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the twentieth year Hideyoshi then divided his forces under the chieftains Yukinaga and Kiyomasa to lead a fleet against Busanjin, secretly crossing the Imjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the twentieth year Hideyoshi dispatched his generals Yukinaga and Kiyomasa with a fleet to press Busanjin, secretly crossing the Imjin River.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮承平久，兵不習戰，昖又湎酒，弛備，猝島夷作難，望風皆潰。

translations.literal: At that time Korea had long enjoyed peace, its troops were unused to war, and Son moreover drowned himself in wine and relaxed defenses; suddenly the island barbarians rose in rebellion, and at sight of them all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Korea had long known peace, its soldiers were unused to war, and Son was given to drink and had let defenses lapse; when the island invaders struck without warning, the armies broke and fled at the first sight of them.

sentences.zh: 昖棄王城，令次子琿攝國事，奔平壤。

translations.literal: Son abandoned the royal capital, ordered his second son Hun to administer state affairs provisionally, and fled to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Son abandoned the capital, entrusted state affairs to his second son Hun, and fled to Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 已，復走義州，願內屬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he fled again to Uiju and expressed the wish to become an inner subject.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he fled again to Uiju and asked to submit to Ming protection.

sentences.zh: 七月，兵部議令駐劄險要，以待天兵；

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Ministry of War deliberated and ordered him to encamp at strategic points and await the Celestial army;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Ministry of War ordered him to hold strategic positions and await the arrival of Ming troops;

sentences.zh: 號召通國勤王，以圖恢復。

translations.literal: rally the whole state to defend the throne, and seek recovery.
translations.idiomatic: rally the whole kingdom to defend the throne and plan for recovery.

sentences.zh: 而是時倭已入王京，毀墳墓，劫王子、陪臣，剽府庫，八道幾盡沒，旦暮且渡鴨綠江，請援之使絡繹於道。

translations.literal: But by then the Wokou had already entered the royal capital, destroyed tombs, seized princes and attending ministers, and plundered treasuries; the eight provinces were nearly all lost, and at any moment they would cross the Yalu River; envoys begging for aid crowded the roads without cease.
translations.idiomatic: But by then the invaders had already entered the capital, desecrated royal tombs, seized princes and ministers, and looted the treasuries; nearly all eight provinces had fallen, and the enemy was poised to cross the Yalu at any moment; pleas for aid crowded the roads without end.

sentences.zh: 廷議以朝鮮為國籓籬，在所必爭。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that Korea was the outer bulwark of the state and a territory that must be contested.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Korea was the outer bulwark of the empire and a territory that must be defended at all costs.

sentences.zh: 遣行人薛潘諭昖以興復大義，揚言大兵十萬且至。

translations.literal: The courier Xue Pan was dispatched to instruct Son in the great principle of restoration, and it was proclaimed that a hundred thousand troops would soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The courier Xue Pan was sent to exhort Son with the duty of restoration, and word was spread that a hundred thousand Ming troops would soon arrive.

sentences.zh: 而倭業抵平壤，朝鮮君臣益急，出避愛州。

translations.literal: But the Wokou had already reached Pyongyang, and the king and ministers of Korea grew ever more desperate and withdrew to Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: But the invaders had already reached Pyongyang, and the Korean king and his ministers, in growing desperation, withdrew to Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遊擊史儒等率師至平壤，戰死。

translations.literal: The guerrilla commander Shi Ru and others led troops to Pyongyang and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The guerrilla commander Shi Ru and others led troops to Pyongyang and were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 副總兵祖承訓統兵渡鴨綠江援之，僅以身免。

translations.literal: The vice commander-in-chief Zu Chengxun led troops across the Yalu River to aid them and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The vice commander Zu Chengxun led troops across the Yalu to their aid and barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 中朝震動，以宋應昌為經略。

translations.literal: The Central Court was shaken, and Song Yingchang was appointed grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The court was shaken, and Song Yingchang was appointed grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 八月，倭入豐德等郡，兵部尚書石星計無所出，議遣人偵探之，於是嘉興人沈惟敬應募。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Wokou entered Haedeok and other districts; the Minister of War Shi Xing could devise no plan and proposed sending someone to reconnoiter; thereupon Shen Weijing of Jiaxing volunteered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the invaders entered Haedeok and other districts; Minister of War Shi Xing could think of no solution and proposed sending a scout; Shen Weijing of Jiaxing volunteered.

sentences.zh: 惟敬者，市中無賴也。

translations.literal: Weijing was a ne'er-do-well of the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing was a marketplace ruffian.

sentences.zh: 是時秀吉次對馬島，分其將行長等守要害為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Hideyoshi was stationed on Tsushima Island and divided his generals such as Yukinaga to hold strategic points as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hideyoshi was stationed on Tsushima and had posted generals such as Yukinaga to hold key positions in support.

sentences.zh: 惟敬至平壤，執禮其卑。

translations.literal: Weijing reached Pyongyang and observed the most abject ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing reached Pyongyang and abased himself in ceremony before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 行長紿曰：「天朝幸按兵不動，我不久當還。

translations.literal: Yukinaga deceived him, saying: "If the Celestial Court will kindly hold its armies in place, I shall not be long in returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga deceived him, saying: "If the Celestial Court will kindly hold its armies in place, I shall withdraw before long.

sentences.zh: 以大同江為界，平壤以西盡屬朝鮮耳。」

translations.literal: Let the Taedong River be the boundary—all west of Pyongyang shall belong to Korea."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Taedong River be the boundary—all lands west of Pyongyang shall remain Korea's."

sentences.zh: 惟敬以聞。

translations.literal: Weijing reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 廷議倭詐未可信，乃趣應昌等進兵。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that the Wokou deception could not be trusted, and Song Yingchang and the others were urged to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged the Japanese offer a deception and urged Song Yingchang and the others to advance.

sentences.zh: 而星頗惑於惟敬，乃題署遊擊，赴軍前，且請金行間。

translations.literal: But Shi Xing was much swayed by Weijing, and so gave him the title of guerrilla commander and sent him to the front, also requesting gold for secret dealings.
translations.idiomatic: But Shi Xing was much taken in by Weijing, commissioned him as a guerrilla commander, and sent him to the front, also supplying gold for covert negotiations.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以李如松為東征提督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Li Rusong was appointed supreme commander of the eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Rusong was appointed supreme commander of the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，如松督諸將進戰，大捷於平壤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Rusong directed the generals in advance and won a great victory at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Rusong led the generals forward and won a great victory at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 行長渡大同江，遁還龍山。

translations.literal: Yukinaga crossed the Taedong River and fled back to Ryongsan.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga crossed the Taedong River and fled back to Ryongsan.

sentences.zh: 所失黃海、平安、京畿、江原四道並復，清正亦遁還王京。

translations.literal: The four lost provinces of Hwanghae, Pyeongan, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon were all recovered, and Kiyomasa also fled back to the royal capital.
translations.idiomatic: The four lost provinces of Hwanghae, Pyeongan, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon were all recovered, and Kiyomasa also retreated to the capital.

sentences.zh: 如松既勝，輕騎趨碧蹄館，敗，退駐開城。

translations.literal: After Rusong's victory he pressed forward with light cavalry to Pyojeok Pavilion, was defeated, and withdrew to garrison Kaesong.
translations.idiomatic: After his victory Rusong pressed forward with light cavalry to Pyojeok Pavilion, was defeated, and withdrew to Kaesong.

sentences.zh: 事具《如松傳》。

translations.literal: The full account is given in the Biography of Rusong.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the Biography of Li Rusong.

sentences.zh: 初，如松誓師，欲斬惟敬，以參軍李應試言而止。

translations.literal: At first, when Rusong swore in the army, he wished to execute Weijing, but desisted on the advice of the staff officer Li Yingshi.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Rusong mustered the army, he wished to execute Weijing, but desisted on the advice of the staff officer Li Yingshi.

sentences.zh: 至是敗，氣縮，而應昌急圖成功，倭亦乏食有歸志，因而封貢之議起。

translations.literal: When he was defeated on this occasion his spirit shrank; Song Yingchang was eager to achieve success, and the Wokou also lacked food and wished to return—thus arose discussion of enfeoffment and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After this defeat his confidence waned; Song Yingchang was eager for a quick success, and the invaders, short of provisions, also wished to withdraw—thus arose talk of enfeoffment and tribute.

sentences.zh: 應昌得倭報惟敬書，乃令遊擊周弘謨同惟敬往諭倭，獻王京，返王子，如約縱歸。

translations.literal: Song Yingchang received a Wokou reply to Weijing's letter and thereupon ordered the guerrilla commander Zhou Hongmo to go with Weijing to instruct the Wokou to surrender the royal capital, return the princes, and release captives as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yingchang received the Japanese reply to Weijing's letter and ordered the guerrilla commander Zhou Hongmo to go with Weijing and instruct the enemy to surrender the capital, return the princes, and release captives as agreed.

sentences.zh: 倭果于四月棄王城遁。

translations.literal: The Wokou indeed abandoned the royal city and fled in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders did abandon the capital and flee in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 時漢江以南千有餘里朝鮮故土復定，兵部言宜令王還國居守，我各鎮兵久疲海外，以次撤歸為便。

translations.literal: At that time more than a thousand li of Korean territory south of the Han River had been recovered; the Ministry of War said the king should be ordered to return and hold the state, while our garrison troops, long exhausted overseas, should be withdrawn in stages for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: By then more than a thousand li of Korean territory south of the Han River had been recovered; the Ministry of War argued that the king should return to hold the kingdom while Ming garrisons, long exhausted overseas, should be withdrawn in stages.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 應昌疏稱：「釜山雖瀕海南，猶朝鮮境，有如倭覘我罷兵，突入再犯，朝鮮不支，前功盡棄。

translations.literal: Song Yingchang submitted a memorial saying: "Although Busan lies on the southern sea, it is still within Korean territory; if the Wokou observe our withdrawal of troops and suddenly invade again, Korea will not be able to hold out and all previous achievements will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yingchang submitted a memorial saying: "Although Busan lies on the southern coast, it is still Korean territory; if the Japanese watch us withdraw and suddenly invade again, Korea will not be able to hold out and all our gains will be lost.

sentences.zh: 今撥兵協守為第一策，即議撤，宜少需，俟倭盡歸，量留防戍。」

translations.literal: To allocate troops for joint defense is now the first strategy; even if withdrawal is discussed, there should be some delay, waiting until the Wokou have all returned, and then leaving a measured force for defense."
translations.idiomatic: Deploying troops for joint defense is the best course; even if withdrawal is discussed, we should wait until the Japanese have fully withdrawn, then leave a measured garrison behind."

sentences.zh: 部議留江浙兵五千，分屯要害，仍諭昖搜練軍實，毋恃外援。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to leave five thousand troops from Jiangsu and Zhejiang, garrisoned at strategic points, and still instructed Son to search out and drill military strength and not rely on external aid.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry decided to leave five thousand troops from Jiangsu and Zhejiang garrisoned at key points, and instructed Son to rebuild and drill his forces rather than rely on outside aid.

sentences.zh: 已而沈惟敬歸自釜山，同倭使來請款，而倭隨犯咸安、晉州，逼全羅，聲復漢江以南，以王京、漢江為界。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Shen Weijing returned from Busan and came with Wokou envoys to sue for peace, but the Wokou then attacked Haman and Jinju, pressed Jeolla, and declared that lands south of the Han River would again be theirs, with the royal capital and the Han River as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shen Weijing returned from Busan with Japanese envoys to sue for peace, but the invaders then attacked Haman and Jinju, pressed into Jeolla, and declared that all lands south of the Han River would be theirs, with the capital and the Han River as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 如松計全羅饒沃，南原府尤其咽喉，乃命諸將分守要害。

translations.literal: Rusong judged that Jeolla was rich and fertile and that Namwon Prefecture was especially its vital passage; he therefore ordered the generals to divide forces and hold strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong judged Jeolla rich and fertile and Namwon Prefecture its vital choke point; he ordered the generals to divide forces and hold the key positions.

sentences.zh: 已，倭果分犯，我師並有斬獲。

translations.literal: Soon the Wokou indeed divided forces to attack, and our armies also had kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the invaders did divide their forces to attack, and Ming troops also scored kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 兵科給事中張輔之、遼東都御史趙耀皆言款貢不可輕受。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Fuzhi and the censor-in-chief of Liaodong Zhao Yao both said that peace and tribute should not be lightly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zhang Fuzhi and the Liaodong censor-in-chief Zhao Yao both argued that peace and tribute should not be accepted lightly.

sentences.zh: 七月，倭從釜山移西生浦，送回王子、陪臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Wokou moved from Busan to Saseongpo and sent back the princes and attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the invaders moved from Busan to Saseongpo and returned the princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 時師久暴露，聞撤，勢難久羈。

translations.literal: At that time the army had long been exposed in the field; on hearing of withdrawal it was hard to keep them long under restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The army had long been exposed in the field; once word of withdrawal spread, it was impossible to keep the troops under control much longer.

sentences.zh: 應昌請留劉綎川兵，吳惟忠、駱尚志等南兵，合薊、遼兵共萬六千，聽綎分佈尚之大丘，月餉五萬兩，資之戶兵二部。

translations.literal: Song Yingchang requested that Liu Ting's Sichuan troops, the southern troops under Wu Weizhong and Luo Shangzhi, and the Ji and Liaodong troops together totaling sixteen thousand be retained, with Ting to distribute them as far as Daegu; monthly rations of fifty thousand taels were to be supplied from the Ministries of Revenue and War.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yingchang asked to retain Liu Ting's Sichuan troops, the southern forces under Wu Weizhong and Luo Shangzhi, and Ji and Liaodong troops totaling sixteen thousand, with Ting to deploy them as far as Daegu; monthly rations of fifty thousand taels were to come from the Ministries of Revenue and War.

sentences.zh: 先是，發帑給軍費，已累百萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, treasury funds had been issued for military expenses, already totaling more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: By then treasury funds issued for military expenses had already exceeded a million taels.

sentences.zh: 廷臣言虛內實外非長策，請以所留川兵命綎訓練，兵餉令本國自辦。

translations.literal: Court officials said that emptying the interior to strengthen the exterior was no long-term strategy and requested that the retained Sichuan troops be ordered to train under Ting while military rations be supplied by the native state itself.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that draining the interior to strengthen the frontier was no long-term strategy and proposed that the retained Sichuan troops train under Liu Ting while Korea itself supply the rations.

sentences.zh: 於是詔撤惟忠等兵，止留綎兵防守。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the withdrawal of the troops under Weizhong and others, retaining only Ting's troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the withdrawal of Wu Weizhong's troops and the others, retaining only Liu Ting's force for defense.

sentences.zh: 諭朝鮮世子臨海君珒居全慶，以顧養謙為經略。

translations.literal: The Korean heir apparent Imhae-gun Gyeong was instructed to reside in Jeolla, and Gu Yangqian was appointed grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The Korean heir apparent Imhae-gun Gyeong was instructed to reside in Jeolla, and Gu Yangqian was appointed grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 九月，昖以三都既復，疆域再造，上表謝恩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Son, because the three capitals had been recovered and the territory restored, submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Son submitted a memorial of thanks, for the three capitals had been recovered and the kingdom restored.

sentences.zh: 然時倭猶據釜山也，星益一意主款。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the Wokou still held Busan, and Shi Xing increasingly insisted on peace alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the invaders still held Busan, and Shi Xing grew ever more committed to peace negotiations alone.

sentences.zh: 九月，兵部主事曾偉芳言：「關白大眾已還，行長留待。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Ministry of War section chief Zeng Weifang said: "The kampaku's main force has already returned; Yukinaga remains waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Ministry of War section chief Zeng Weifang said: "The regent's main force has already returned; Yukinaga remains behind.

sentences.zh: 知我兵未撤，不敢以一矢加遺。

translations.literal: Knowing our troops have not withdrawn, he dares not add a single arrow to those left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing our troops have not yet withdrawn, he dares not launch a single attack.

sentences.zh: 欲歸報關白捲土重來，則風不利，正苦冬寒。

translations.literal: If he wishes to return and report to the kampaku to gather forces and come again, the winds are unfavorable and winter cold is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: If he wishes to return and report to the regent to gather forces and invade again, the winds are unfavorable and winter cold is bitter.

sentences.zh: 故款亦去，不款亦去。

translations.literal: Thus whether there is peace he will leave, and whether there is no peace he will also leave.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we make peace or not, he will leave either way.

sentences.zh: 沈惟敬前于倭營講購，咸安、晉州隨陷，而俗恃款冀來年不攻，則速之款者，正速之來耳。

translations.literal: When Shen Weijing earlier negotiated purchase in the Wokou camp, Haman and Jinju soon fell; yet people rely on peace and hope there will be no attack next year—then those who hurry peace are precisely hurrying the coming attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Weijing earlier negotiated in the Japanese camp, Haman and Jinju soon fell; yet people cling to hopes of peace and expect no attack next year—those who rush toward peace are precisely rushing toward the next invasion.

sentences.zh: 故款亦來，不款亦來。

translations.literal: Thus whether there is peace they will come, and whether there is no peace they will also come.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we make peace or not, they will come either way.

sentences.zh: 宜令朝鮮自為守，吊死問孤，練兵積粟，以圖自強。」

translations.literal: Korea should be ordered to defend itself, comfort the dead and inquire after the orphaned, drill troops and store grain, and seek self-strengthening."
translations.idiomatic: Korea should be ordered to defend itself, tend the dead and care for the bereaved, drill troops and store grain, and seek to grow strong on its own."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，因敕諭昖者甚至。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this correct and therefore issued edicts instructing Son at great length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued lengthy edicts instructing Son accordingly.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月，昖遣金晬等進方物謝恩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year Son dispatched Jin Chui and others to present local products in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-second year Son dispatched Jin Chui and others to present tribute in thanks.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中何喬遠奏：「晬涕泣言倭寇猖獗，朝鮮束手受刃者六萬餘人。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites bureau director He Qiaoyuan submitted a memorial: "Chui wept and said the Wokou were rampant and that more than sixty thousand persons in Korea had been slaughtered without resistance.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites bureau director He Qiaoyuan submitted a memorial: "Chui wept and reported that the pirates were rampant and that more than sixty thousand Koreans had been slaughtered without resistance.

sentences.zh: 倭語悖慢無禮，沈惟敬與倭交通，不雲和親，輒曰乞降。

translations.literal: Wokou speech was insolent and without propriety; Shen Weijing trafficked with the Wokou and, rather than speaking of marriage alliance, kept saying they begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese envoys spoke with insolent disrespect; Shen Weijing had dealings with them and, rather than speak of alliance, kept saying they were begging to surrender.

sentences.zh: 臣謹將萬曆十九年中國被掠人許儀所寄內地書、倭夷答劉綎書及歷年入寇處置之宜，乞特敕急止封貢。」

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully submits the letter sent inland by Xu Yi, a person seized from China in the nineteenth year of Wanli, the Wokou reply to Liu Ting, and what should be done about invasions over the years, and begs a special edict urgently to halt enfeoffment and tribute."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully submits the letter sent inland by Xu Yi, a Chinese captive from the nineteenth year of Wanli, the Japanese reply to Liu Ting, and recommendations on handling the invasions over the years, and begs a special edict urgently halting enfeoffment and tribute."

sentences.zh: 詔兵部議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of War to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of War to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣交章，皆以罷封貢、議戰守為言。

translations.literal: At that time court officials submitted memorial after memorial, all speaking of abolishing enfeoffment and tribute and discussing war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time officials submitted memorial after memorial, all urging an end to enfeoffment and tribute and calling for renewed discussion of war and defense.

sentences.zh: 八月，養謙奏講貢之說，貢道宜從寧波，關白宜封為日本王，諭行長部倭盡歸，與封貢如約。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yangqian submitted the plan for negotiated tribute: the tribute route should be through Ningbo, the kampaku should be enfeoffed as King of Japan, Yukinaga's Wokou should be instructed to return entirely, and enfeoffment and tribute should proceed as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Gu Yangqian submitted a plan for negotiated tribute: the tribute route should run through Ningbo, the regent should be enfeoffed as King of Japan, Yukinaga's forces should be ordered to withdraw entirely, and enfeoffment and tribute should proceed as agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，昖請許保國。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Son requested permission to preserve the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Son petitioned for assurance that his kingdom would be preserved.

sentences.zh: 帝乃切責群臣阻撓，追褫御史郭實等。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon sharply rebuked the officials for obstruction and stripped Censor Guo Shi and others of their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked the officials for obstruction and stripped Censor Guo Shi and others of their posts.

sentences.zh: 詔小西飛入朝，集多官面議，要以三事：一，勒倭盡歸巢；

translations.literal: An edict summoned Konishi Yukufusa to court, gathered many officials for face-to-face deliberation, and required three things: first, compel the Wokou to return entirely to their nests;
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Konishi Yukufusa to court, gathered senior officials for face-to-face deliberation, and set three conditions: first, compel the Japanese to withdraw entirely;

sentences.zh: 一，既封不與貢；

translations.literal: second, once enfeoffed, no tribute would be granted;
translations.idiomatic: second, once enfeoffed, no tribute would be accepted;

sentences.zh: 一，誓無犯朝鮮。

translations.literal: third, swear not to violate Korea.
translations.idiomatic: third, swear never again to invade Korea.

sentences.zh: 倭俱聽從，以聞。

translations.literal: The Wokou all obeyed, and this was reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese envoys agreed to all three, and this was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝復諭于左闕，語加周復。

translations.literal: The Emperor again instructed them at the Left Gate, his words becoming ever more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again addressed them at the Left Gate, his instructions growing ever more detailed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，封議定，命臨淮侯李宗城充正使，以都指揮楊方亨副之，同沈惟敬往日本，王給金印，行長授都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the enfeoffment plan was settled; Marquis of Linhuai Li Zongcheng was appointed chief envoy, with Commander Yang Fangheng as deputy, to go with Shen Weijing to Japan; a golden seal was granted to the king, and Yukinaga was appointed Assistant Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the enfeoffment plan was settled; Marquis of Linhuai Li Zongcheng was appointed chief envoy, with Commander Yang Fangheng as deputy, to travel with Shen Weijing to Japan; a golden seal was granted to the Japanese king, and Yukinaga was appointed Assistant Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十三年九月，昖奏立次子琿為嗣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-third year Son submitted a memorial to establish his second son Hun as heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-third year Son petitioned to establish his second son Hun as heir.

sentences.zh: 先是，昖庶長子臨海君珒陷賊中，驚憂成疾，次子光海君琿收集流散，頗著功績，奏請立之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Son's eldest son by a concubine, Imhae-gun Gyeong, had fallen into enemy hands, and shock and grief had brought on illness; the second son Gwanghae-gun Hun gathered the scattered populace and achieved considerable merit, and a memorial requested his establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Son's eldest son by a concubine, Imhae-gun Gyeong, had fallen into enemy hands; shock and grief had brought on illness; the second son Gwanghae-gun Hun had gathered the scattered populace and won considerable merit, and a memorial requested that he be made heir.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書范謙言繼統大義，長幼定分，不宜僭差，遂不許。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites Fan Qian said that the great principle of succession and the fixed order of elder and younger should not be violated by usurpation, and permission was therefore denied.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Fan Qian argued that the principle of succession and the fixed order of elder and younger must not be violated, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 至是復奏，引永樂間恭定王例上請，禮臣執奏，不從。

translations.literal: On this occasion he submitted again, citing the precedent of King Gongding in the Yongle reign and requesting approval from above; the ritual officials submitted firm memorials and the court did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he submitted again, citing the precedent of King Gongding in the Yongle reign; the ritual officials submitted firm objections and the court did not comply.

sentences.zh: 二十四年五月，昖復疏請立琿，禮部仍執不可，詔如議。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year Son again submitted a memorial requesting Hun's establishment; the Ministry of Rites still held that it could not be done, and an edict followed the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year Son again petitioned to establish Hun; the Ministry of Rites still held firm against it, and an edict followed their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時國儲未建，中外恫疑，故尚書范謙于朝鮮易封事三疏力持雲。

translations.literal: At that time the heir to the state had not been established and court and country alike were uneasy; hence Minister Fan Qian submitted three memorials on Korea's succession dispute and forcefully maintained his position.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no crown prince had been established and court and country alike were uneasy; hence Minister Fan Qian submitted three memorials on Korea's succession dispute and held firmly to his position.

sentences.zh: 九月，封使至日本。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the enfeoffment envoys reached Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the investiture mission arrived in Japan.

sentences.zh: 先是，沈惟敬抵釜山，私奉秀吉蟒玉、翼善冠、地圖、武經、良馬。

translations.literal: Previously, Shen Weijing had reached Busan and privately presented Hideyoshi with python-pattern jade, the Yishan cap, maps, military classics, and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shen Weijing had reached Busan and on his own authority had presented Hideyoshi with python-pattern jade, the Yishan cap, maps, military treatises, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 而李宗城以貪淫為倭守臣所逐，棄璽書夜遁。

translations.literal: But Li Zongcheng, on account of greed and debauchery, was driven off by the Japanese garrison commanders; he abandoned the imperial patent and edicts and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongcheng, however, had been driven off by the Japanese garrison commanders for his greed and debauchery; he abandoned the imperial patent and edicts and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 事聞，逮問。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was arrested and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, he was arrested and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 乃以方亨充正使，加惟敬神機營銜副之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Fangheng was appointed chief envoy, with Weijing given the title of deputy from the Shenji Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fangheng was then appointed chief envoy, with Weijing added as deputy bearing a Shenji Camp commission.

sentences.zh: 及是奉冊至，關白怒朝鮮王子不來謝，止遣二使奉白土綢為賀，拒其使不見，語惟敬曰：「若不思二子、三大臣、三都、八道悉遵天朝約付還，今以卑官微物來賀，辱小邦邪？

translations.literal: When the investiture patent was presented, the Kampaku was enraged that the Korean princes had not come to offer thanks; he sent only two envoys bearing white silk from Suzhou as congratulations, refused to receive the Ming envoys, and told Weijing: "If you do not consider that the two princes, the three ministers, the three capitals, and the eight provinces should all be surrendered according to the Celestial Court's agreement, and now you come with a lowly official bearing paltry gifts to offer congratulations—is this to insult our little realm?
translations.idiomatic: When the investiture patent was delivered, the regent was furious that no Korean princes had come to give thanks; he sent only two envoys with Suzhou white silk as congratulatory gifts, refused to receive the Ming mission, and told Weijing: "If you have no thought of restoring the two princes, the three ministers, the three capitals, and the eight provinces as the Celestial Court agreed, and now send a petty official with trifling gifts to congratulate us—is this meant to insult our realm?

sentences.zh: 辱天朝邪？

translations.literal: Or to insult the Celestial Court?
translations.idiomatic: Or to insult the Celestial Court itself?

sentences.zh: 且留石曼子兵於彼，候天朝處分，然後撤還。」

translations.literal: Moreover, I shall leave Shimazu's troops there to await the Celestial Court's disposition, and only then withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I shall leave Shimazu's troops there to await the Celestial Court's decision, and only then withdraw them.

sentences.zh: 翌日奉貢，遣使齎表文二道，隨冊使渡海至朝鮮。

translations.literal: The next day he presented tribute and dispatched envoys carrying two memorials, who crossed the sea with the investiture envoys to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he offered tribute and sent envoys bearing two memorials, who crossed the sea with the investiture mission to Korea.

sentences.zh: 廷議遣使於朝鮮，取表文進驗，其一謝恩，其一乞天子處分朝鮮。

translations.literal: The court deliberated on sending envoys to Korea to obtain the memorials for inspection: one was a thanksgiving memorial, the other begged the Son of Heaven to dispose of Korea.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated sending envoys to Korea to retrieve the memorials for examination: one was a thanksgiving petition, the other asked the Son of Heaven to settle Korea's fate.

sentences.zh: 初，方亨詭報去年從釜山渡海，倭於大版受封，即回和泉州。

translations.literal: At first Fangheng had falsely reported that last year he had crossed from Busan, the Japanese had received enfeoffment at Osaka, and he had returned via Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fangheng had falsely reported that the previous year he had crossed from Busan, the Japanese had received investiture at Osaka, and he had returned by way of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 然倭方責備朝鮮，仍留兵釜山如故，謝表後時不發，方亨徒手歸。

translations.literal: Yet the Japanese were still pressing claims against Korea and continued to hold troops at Busan as before; the thanksgiving memorial was never sent in time, and Fangheng returned empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Japanese were still pressing demands against Korea and kept troops at Busan as before; the thanksgiving memorial was never dispatched in time, and Fangheng returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 至是，惟敬始投表文，案驗潦草，前折用豐臣圖書，不奉正朔，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: At this point Weijing finally submitted the memorials; on examination they were perfunctory, and earlier he had used Toyotomi seals and documents, failed to adopt the court calendar, and showed none of the protocol due a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did Weijing submit the memorials; on inspection they proved perfunctory, and he had earlier used Toyotomi seals and documents, refused to observe the court calendar, and displayed none of a subject's proper deference.

sentences.zh: 而寬奠副總兵馬楝報清正擁二百艘屯機張營。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Vice Regional Commander Ma Dong of Kuandian reported that Kiyomasa commanded two hundred ships and was encamped at Gijang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Vice Regional Commander Ma Dong at Kuandian reported that Kiyomasa had two hundred ships and was encamped at Gijang.

sentences.zh: 方亨始直吐本末，委罪惟敬，並呈石星前後手書。

translations.literal: Fangheng now for the first time told the whole truth straight out, laid the blame on Weijing, and submitted Shi Xing's letters back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Fangheng at last told the whole story plainly, shifted the blame onto Weijing, and submitted Shi Xing's correspondence.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命逮石星、沈惟敬案問。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and ordered Shi Xing and Shen Weijing arrested and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered Shi Xing and Shen Weijing arrested for investigation.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書邢玠總督薊、遼；

translations.literal: Minister of War Xing Jie was appointed grand coordinator of Ji and Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Xing Jie was appointed grand coordinator of Ji and Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 改麻貴為備倭大將軍，經理朝鮮；

translations.literal: Ma Gui was reassigned as Grand General for Defense against the Wokou, to administer affairs in Korea;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui was reassigned as Grand General for Defense against the Japanese, to manage affairs in Korea;

sentences.zh: 僉都御史楊鎬駐天津，申警備；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yang Hao was stationed at Tianjin to raise the alarm and ready defenses;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Hao was posted at Tianjin to sound the alarm and prepare defenses;

sentences.zh: 楊汝南、丁應泰贊畫軍前。

translations.literal: Yang Runan and Ding Yingtai served as military secretaries at the front.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Runan and Ding Yingtai served as staff officers at the front.

sentences.zh: 五月，玠至遼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xing Jie reached Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xing Jie reached Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 行長建樓，清正布種，島倭窖水，索朝鮮地圖，玠遂決意用兵。

translations.literal: Yukinaga built towers, Kiyomasa sowed seed, the island invaders stored water, and demanded Korean maps; Xing Jie thereupon resolved to use force.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga built watchtowers, Kiyomasa planted crops, the island invaders stockpiled water, and demanded maps of Korea; Xing Jie thereupon resolved on war.

sentences.zh: 麻貴望鴨綠江東發，所統兵僅萬七千人，請濟師。

translations.literal: Ma Gui looked to advance from across the Yalu River; the troops under his command numbered only seventeen thousand, and he requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui looked to advance from east of the Yalu River, but the troops under his command numbered only seventeen thousand, and he requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 玠以朝鮮兵惟嫻水戰，乃疏請募兵川、浙，並調薊、遼、宣、大、山、陝兵及福建、吳淞水師，劉綎督川、漢兵聽剿。

translations.literal: Xing Jie held that Korean troops were skilled only in naval warfare; he memorialized requesting recruitment from Sichuan and Zhejiang, and mobilization of troops from Ji, Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, Shandong, Shaanxi, the Fujian navy, and the Wusong fleet, with Liu Ting to command the Sichuan and Huguang forces for suppression operations.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie held that Korean troops were skilled only at naval warfare; he memorialized requesting recruits from Sichuan and Zhejiang, and the mobilization of troops from Ji, Liaodong, Xuanfu, Datong, Shandong, and Shaanxi, along with the Fujian and Wusong fleets, with Liu Ting to command the Sichuan and Huguang forces for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 貴密報候宣、大兵至，乘倭未備，掩釜山，則行長擒，清正走。

translations.literal: Ma Gui secretly reported that when the Xuanfu and Datong troops arrived, they could seize Busan while the Japanese were unprepared; Yukinaga would be captured and Kiyomasa would flee.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui secretly reported that once the Xuanfu and Datong troops arrived, they could strike Busan while the Japanese were unprepared—Yukinaga would be captured and Kiyomasa would flee.

sentences.zh: 玠以為奇計，乃檄楊元屯南原，吳惟忠屯忠州。

translations.literal: Xing Jie thought this a brilliant stratagem and issued orders for Yang Yuan to encamp at Namwon and Wu Weizhong at Chungju.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie thought this a brilliant plan and ordered Yang Yuan to encamp at Namwon and Wu Weizhong at Chungju.

sentences.zh: 六月，倭數千艘泊釜山，戮朝鮮郡守安弘國，漸逼梁山、熊川。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, thousands of Japanese ships anchored at Busan; they killed the Korean prefect An Hongguk and gradually pressed toward Yangsan and Ungcheon.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month thousands of Japanese ships anchored at Busan; they killed the Korean prefect An Hongguk and gradually pressed toward Yangsan and Ungcheon.

sentences.zh: 惟敬率營兵二百，出入釜山。

translations.literal: Weijing led two hundred camp troops in and out of Busan.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing led two hundred camp troops in and out of Busan.

sentences.zh: 玠陽為慰藉，檄楊元襲執之，縛至貴營，惟敬執而嚮導始絕。

translations.literal: Xing Jie feigned conciliation, ordered Yang Yuan to seize Weijing in a surprise raid, bound him, and sent him to Ma Gui's camp; once Weijing was captive, the Japanese guides were cut off for good.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie feigned conciliation, ordered Yang Yuan to seize Weijing in a surprise raid, had him bound and sent to Ma Gui's camp, and with Weijing in custody the Japanese guides were cut off at last.

sentences.zh: 七月，倭奪梁山、三浪，遂入慶州，侵閑山。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Japanese took Yangsan and Sannang, then entered Gyeongju and invaded Hansan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Japanese took Yangsan and Sannang, entered Gyeongju, and invaded Hansan.

sentences.zh: 統制元均兵潰，遂失閑山。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Won Kyun's army collapsed, and Hansan was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Won Kyun's army collapsed, and Hansan was lost.

sentences.zh: 閑山島在朝鮮西海口，右障南原，為全羅外籓，一失守則沿海無備，天津、登、萊皆可揚帆而至。

translations.literal: Hansan Island lies at the western sea mouth of Korea; on the right it shields Namwon and forms the outer bulwark of Jeolla; once it fell the entire coast was undefended, and Tianjin, Dengzhou, and Laizhou could all be reached under sail.
translations.idiomatic: Hansan Island stood at Korea's western sea gate, shielding Namwon on the right and forming Jeolla's outer defense; once it fell the entire coast lay open, and Tianjin, Dengzhou, and Laizhou could all be reached under sail.

sentences.zh: 而我水兵三千甫抵旅順，閑山破，經略檄守王京西之漢江、大同江，扼倭西下，兼防運道。

translations.literal: Our three thousand naval troops had only just reached Lüshun when Hansan fell; the supreme commander issued orders to hold the Han River and Daedong River west of the capital, blocking the Japanese advance westward while also protecting the supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Our three thousand naval troops had only just reached Lüshun when Hansan fell; the supreme commander ordered troops to hold the Han and Daedong rivers west of the capital, blocking the Japanese advance westward while protecting the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 八月，清正圍南原，乘夜猝攻，守將楊元遁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Kiyomasa besieged Namwon, attacked suddenly by night, and the defending general Yang Yuan fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Kiyomasa besieged Namwon and attacked by surprise in the night; the defending general Yang Yuan fled.

sentences.zh: 時全州有陳愚衷，去南原僅百里，南原告急，愚衷不敢救，聞已破，棄城走。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Yuzhong was at Jeonju, only a hundred li from Namwon; when Namwon cried for help, Yuzhong dared not go to the rescue, and when he heard it had fallen, he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen Yuzhong was at Jeonju, only a hundred li from Namwon; when Namwon cried for help Yuzhong dared not go to the rescue, and when he heard it had fallen he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 麻貴遣遊擊牛伯英赴援，與愚衷合兵，屯公州。

translations.literal: Ma Gui sent guerrilla commander Niu Boying to the rescue; he joined forces with Yuzhong and encamped at Gongju.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui sent guerrilla commander Niu Boying to the rescue; he joined forces with Yuzhong and encamped at Gongju.

sentences.zh: 倭遂犯全慶，逼王京。

translations.literal: The Japanese then attacked Jeonju and Gyeongju and pressed toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese then attacked Jeonju and Gyeongju and pressed toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 王京為朝鮮八道之中，東阻烏嶺、忠州，西則南原、全州，道相通。

translations.literal: The capital stood at the center of Korea's eight provinces; to the east it was blocked by Oryong and Chungju, to the west lay Namwon and Jeonju, and the routes connected.
translations.idiomatic: The capital stood at the center of Korea's eight provinces; to the east it was shielded by Oryong and Chungju, to the west lay Namwon and Jeonju, and the roads linked them all.

sentences.zh: 自二城失，東西皆倭，我兵單弱，因退守王京，依險漢江。
