translations.literal: With the loss of these two cities, Japanese forces lay to east and west alike; our troops were few and weak, so we fell back to hold the capital, relying on the Han River as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: With the loss of these two cities, Japanese forces lay to east and west alike; our troops were few and weak, so we fell back to hold the capital behind the Han River's natural defenses.

sentences.zh: 麻貴請於玠欲棄王京退守鴨綠江。

translations.literal: Ma Gui requested of Xing Jie that they abandon the capital and withdraw to hold the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui asked Xing Jie to abandon the capital and withdraw to hold the Yalu River.

sentences.zh: 海防使蕭應宮以為不可，自平壤兼程趨王京止之。

translations.literal: Coastal Defense Commissioner Xiao Yinggong held this impossible; he hurried from Pyongyang day and night to the capital to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal Defense Commissioner Xiao Yinggong thought this impossible and hurried from Pyongyang day and night to the capital to stop it.

sentences.zh: 麻貴發兵守稷山，朝鮮亦調都體察使李元翼由烏嶺出忠清道遮賊鋒。

translations.literal: Ma Gui dispatched troops to hold Jisan; Korea also mobilized Inspector-General Yi Won-ik to emerge from Oryong into Chungcheong Province to block the enemy vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui dispatched troops to hold Jisan; Korea also mobilized Inspector-General Yi Won-ik to emerge from Oryong into Chungcheong Province and block the enemy vanguard.

sentences.zh: 玠既身赴王京，人心始定。

translations.literal: Once Xing Jie himself went to the capital, the people's hearts at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xing Jie went to the capital in person, morale at last steadied.

sentences.zh: 玠召參軍李應試問計，應試請問廟廷主畫雲何。

translations.literal: Xing Jie summoned staff officer Li Yingshi to ask his counsel; Yingshi asked what the court's secret strategy was.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie summoned staff officer Li Yingshi to ask his counsel; Yingshi asked what the court's secret plan was.

sentences.zh: 玠曰：「陽戰陰和，陽剿陰撫，政府八字密畫，無泄也。

translations.literal: Xing Jie said: "Open war and secret peace, open suppression and secret appeasement—the government's eight-character secret plan must not be disclosed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie said: "Open war and secret peace, open suppression and secret appeasement—the government's eight-character secret plan must not be disclosed.

sentences.zh: 應試曰：「然則易耳。

translations.literal: Yingshi said: "Then it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi said: "Then it is easy.

sentences.zh: 倭叛以處分絕望，其不敢殺楊元，猶望處分也。

translations.literal: The Japanese have rebelled because they despair of receiving imperial disposition; they have not dared kill Yang Yuan because they still hope for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese have rebelled because they despair of receiving an imperial settlement; they have not dared kill Yang Yuan because they still hope for one.

sentences.zh: 直使人諭之曰沈惟敬不死，則退矣。」

translations.literal: Simply send someone to tell them: if Shen Weijing is not executed, they will withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Simply send someone to tell them: if Shen Weijing is not executed, they will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 因請使李大諫于行長，馮仲纓於清正，玠從之。

translations.literal: He therefore requested sending Li Dajian to Yukinaga and Feng Zhongying to Kiyomasa; Xing Jie agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed sending Li Dajian to Yukinaga and Feng Zhongying to Kiyomasa, and Xing Jie agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，倭至漢江，楊鎬遣張貞明持惟敬手書往，責其動兵，有乖靜候處分之實。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Japanese reached the Han River; Yang Hao sent Zhang Zhenming bearing Weijing's handwritten letter to reprimand them for taking up arms, which violated their pledge to wait quietly for imperial disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Japanese reached the Han River; Yang Hao sent Zhang Zhenming with Weijing's handwritten letter to rebuke them for taking up arms, which violated their pledge to wait quietly for an imperial settlement.

sentences.zh: 行長、正成亦尤清正輕舉，乃退屯井邑。

translations.literal: Yukinaga and Masamori also reproached Kiyomasa for his rash action, and withdrew to encamp at Jeongnyeong.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga and Masamori also reproached Kiyomasa for his rash action and withdrew to encamp at Jeongnyeong.

sentences.zh: 麻貴遂報青山、稷山大捷。

translations.literal: Ma Gui then reported a great victory at Cheongsan and Jisan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui then reported a great victory at Cheongsan and Jisan.

sentences.zh: 蕭應宮揭言：「倭以惟敬手書而退，青山、稷山並未接戰，何得言功？」

translations.literal: Xiao Yinggong openly declared: "The Japanese withdrew because of Weijing's letter; at Cheongsan and Jisan there was no engagement at all—how can this be claimed as merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yinggong openly declared: "The Japanese withdrew because of Weijing's letter; at Cheongsan and Jisan there was no engagement at all—how can this be claimed as merit?"

sentences.zh: 玠、鎬怒，遂劾應宮恇怯，不親解惟敬，並逮。

translations.literal: Xing Jie and Yang Hao were enraged and impeached Yinggong for cowardice and for not personally interceding for Weijing; Yinggong was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie and Yang Hao were enraged and impeached Yinggong for cowardice and for not personally going to negotiate over Weijing; Yinggong was arrested.

sentences.zh: 十一月，玠徵兵大集，帝發帑金犒軍，賜玠尚方劍，而以御史陳效監其軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, as Xing Jie's mobilized troops assembled in force, the emperor released treasury gold to reward the army, bestowed on Xing Jie the imperial sword, and appointed Censor Chen Xiao to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, as Xing Jie's mobilized troops assembled in force, the emperor released treasury gold to reward the army, bestowed the imperial sword on Xing Jie, and appointed Censor Chen Xiao to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 玠大會諸將，分三協。

translations.literal: Xing Jie convened the generals in great council and divided them into three divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie convened the generals in great council and divided them into three divisions.

sentences.zh: 鎬同貴率左右協，自忠州、烏嶺向東安，趨慶州，專攻清正。

translations.literal: Yang Hao together with Ma Gui led the left and right divisions from Chungju and Oryong toward Dongan, pressing toward Gyeongju, exclusively to attack Kiyomasa.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao together with Ma Gui led the left and right divisions from Chungju and Oryong toward Dongan, pressing toward Gyeongju to attack Kiyomasa exclusively.

sentences.zh: 使李大諫通行長，約勿往援。

translations.literal: Li Dajian was sent to Yukinaga to agree that he would not come to Kiyomasa's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dajian was sent to Yukinaga with an agreement that he would not come to Kiyomasa's aid.

sentences.zh: 復遣中協屯宜城，東援慶州，西扼全羅。

translations.literal: The center division was again dispatched to encamp at Uijeong, supporting Gyeongju to the east and blocking Jeolla to the west.
translations.idiomatic: The center division was again dispatched to encamp at Uijeong, supporting Gyeongju to the east and blocking Jeolla to the west.

sentences.zh: 以餘兵會朝鮮合營，詐攻順天等處，以牽制行長東援。

translations.literal: The remaining troops joined the Korean combined camp and feigned attacks on Suncheon and other places to tie down Yukinaga's eastern relief.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining troops joined the Korean combined camp and feigned attacks on Suncheon and other places to tie down Yukinaga's eastern relief force.

sentences.zh: 十二月，會慶州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they assembled at Gyeongju.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they assembled at Gyeongju.

sentences.zh: 麻貴遣黃慶賜賄清正約和，而率大兵奄至其營。

translations.literal: Ma Gui sent Huang Qing with bribes to Kiyomasa to negotiate peace, while leading a great force to pounce on his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui sent Huang Qing with bribes to Kiyomasa to negotiate peace, while leading a great force to pounce on his camp.

sentences.zh: 時倭屯蔚山，城依山險，中一江通釜寨，其陸路由彥陽通釜山。

translations.literal: At the time the Japanese were encamped at Ulsan; the fortress stood on mountainous terrain, a river in the middle linked to the Busan stockade, and the overland route from Ulsan connected to Busan via Uiryang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Japanese were encamped at Ulsan; the fortress stood on mountainous terrain with a river in the middle linking to the Busan garrison, and the overland route from Uiryang connected to Busan.

sentences.zh: 貴欲專攻蔚山，恐釜倭由彥陽來援，乃多張疑兵，又遣將遏其水路，遂進逼倭壘。

translations.literal: Ma Gui wished to concentrate on attacking Ulsan but feared Japanese from Busan would come to the rescue via Uiryang; he therefore deployed many dummy forces, also sent generals to block the water route, and then pressed close to the enemy fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui wished to concentrate on attacking Ulsan but feared Japanese from Busan would come to the rescue via Uiryang; he therefore deployed many decoy forces, sent generals to block the water route, and then pressed close to the enemy fortifications.

sentences.zh: 遊擊擺寨以輕騎誘倭入伏，斬級四百餘，獲其勇將，乘勝拔兩柵。

translations.literal: Guerrilla commander Bai Zhai lured the Japanese into an ambush with light cavalry, beheaded more than four hundred, captured an enemy brave general, and following up the victory seized two palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla commander Bai Zhai lured the Japanese into an ambush with light cavalry, beheaded more than four hundred, captured one of their brave generals, and following up the victory seized two palisades.

sentences.zh: 倭焚死者無算，遂奔島山，連築三寨。

translations.literal: Countless Japanese died in the fire; they then fled to Island Mountain and built three camps in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Countless Japanese died in the fire; they then fled to Island Mountain and built three camps in succession.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遊擊茅國器統浙兵先登，連破之，斬獲甚多，倭堅壁不出。

translations.literal: The next day guerrilla commander Mao Guoqi leading Zhejiang troops scaled the walls first; they broke through in succession, killing and capturing greatly, but the Japanese held fast behind their walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day guerrilla commander Mao Guoqi leading Zhejiang troops scaled the walls first; they broke through in succession with many kills and captures, but the Japanese held fast behind their walls and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 島山視蔚山高，石城堅甚，我師仰攻多損傷。

translations.literal: Island Mountain overlooked Ulsan and was higher; the stone walls were very strong, and our troops suffered many casualties in uphill assaults.
translations.idiomatic: Island Mountain overlooked Ulsan and stood higher; the stone walls were very strong, and our troops suffered many casualties in uphill assaults.

sentences.zh: 諸將乃議曰：「倭艱水道，餉難繼，第坐困之，清正可不戰縛也。」

translations.literal: The generals then deliberated: "The Japanese have difficulty with the water route and supplies will be hard to sustain; we need only sit and wear them down, and Kiyomasa can be bound without battle.
translations.idiomatic: The generals then deliberated: "The Japanese have difficulty with the water route and supplies will be hard to sustain; we need only sit and wear them down, and Kiyomasa can be taken without a fight.

sentences.zh: 鎬等以為然，分兵圍十日夜，倭饑甚，偽約降緩攻。

translations.literal: Yang Hao and the others agreed; they divided forces and besieged for ten days and nights; the Japanese were starving greatly and feigned surrender to slow the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao and the others agreed; they divided forces and besieged for ten days and nights; the Japanese were starving badly and feigned surrender to slow the assault.

sentences.zh: 俄行長援兵大至，將繞出軍後。

translations.literal: Suddenly Yukinaga's relief force arrived in strength and was about to circle behind the army.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Yukinaga's relief force arrived in strength and was about to circle behind the army.

sentences.zh: 鎬不及下令，策馬西奔，諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: Yang Hao could not even issue orders; he whipped his horse and fled west, and all the armies collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao could not even issue orders; he whipped his horse and fled west, and all the armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 遂撤兵還王京，士卒物故者二萬。

translations.literal: They withdrew to the capital; twenty thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to the capital; twenty thousand soldiers perished.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，震怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was shaken with rage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he was shaken with rage.

sentences.zh: 乃罷鎬聽勘，以天津巡撫萬世德代。

translations.literal: Yang Hao was dismissed pending investigation and replaced by Tianjin Grand Coordinator Wan Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao was dismissed pending investigation and replaced by Tianjin Grand Coordinator Wan Shide.

sentences.zh: 事詳《鎬傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in Yang Hao's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is detailed in Yang Hao's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十六年正月，邢玠以前役乏水兵無功，乃益募江南水兵，議海運，為持久計。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-sixth year, Xing Jie, because the previous campaign had lacked naval troops and achieved nothing, increased recruitment of Jiangnan naval forces, proposed sea transport of supplies, and planned for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-sixth year, Xing Jie, because the previous campaign had lacked naval troops and achieved nothing, increased recruitment of Jiangnan naval forces, proposed sea transport of supplies, and planned for a prolonged campaign.

sentences.zh: 二月，都督陳璘以廣兵，劉綎以川兵，鄧子龍以浙、直兵先後至。

translations.literal: In the second month Admiral Chen Lin arrived with Guangdong troops, Liu Ting with Sichuan troops, and Deng Zilong with Zhejiang and direct-command troops, arriving one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Admiral Chen Lin arrived with Guangdong troops, Liu Ting with Sichuan troops, and Deng Zilong with Zhejiang and direct-command troops, arriving one after another.

sentences.zh: 玠分兵三協，為水陸四路，路置大將。

translations.literal: Xing Jie divided the forces into three divisions, forming four routes by land and sea, each route with its own commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jie divided the forces into three divisions, forming four routes by land and sea, each with its own commander.

sentences.zh: 中路如梅，東路貴，西路綎，水路璘，各守汛地，相機行剿。

translations.literal: The center route: Li Rumei; eastern route: Ma Gui; western route: Liu Ting; naval route: Chen Lin—each held his assigned sector and undertook suppression as opportunity offered.
translations.idiomatic: The center route was Li Rumei, the eastern route Ma Gui, the western route Liu Ting, and the naval route Chen Lin—each held his assigned sector and undertook suppression as opportunity offered.

sentences.zh: 時倭亦分三窟。

translations.literal: At the time the Japanese also divided into three lairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Japanese also divided into three strongholds.

sentences.zh: 東路則清正，據蔚山。

translations.literal: The eastern route: Kiyomasa, holding Ulsan.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern route Kiyomasa held Ulsan.

sentences.zh: 西路則行長，據粟林、曳橋，建砦數重。

translations.literal: The western route: Yukinaga, holding Surim and Yegeo, building fortifications layer upon layer.
translations.idiomatic: On the western route Yukinaga held Surim and Yegeo, building fortifications layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 中路則石曼子，據泗州。

translations.literal: The center route: Shimazu, holding Sacheon.
translations.idiomatic: On the center route Shimazu held Sacheon.

sentences.zh: 而行長水師番休濟餉，往來如駛。

translations.literal: Yukinaga's navy rotated in shifts to deliver supplies, coming and going like flying arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga's navy rotated in shifts to deliver supplies, coming and going like flying arrows.

sentences.zh: 我師約日並進，尋報遼陽警，李如松敗沒，詔如梅還赴之，中路以董一元代。

translations.literal: Our forces agreed on a date to advance together; soon came word of an alarm at Liaoyang—Li Rusong had been defeated and killed; an edict ordered Li Rumei to return to respond; Dong Yiyuan replaced him on the center route.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces agreed on a date to advance together; soon came word of an alarm at Liaoyang—Li Rusong had been defeated and killed; an edict ordered Li Rumei to return to respond, and Dong Yiyuan replaced him on the center route.

sentences.zh: 當應泰之劾鎬也，昖請回乾斷，崇勵鎮撫，以畢征討。

translations.literal: When Ding Yingtai impeached Yang Hao, Son petitioned for the emperor's own judgment, urging encouragement and reassurance, so that the campaign might be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Yingtai impeached Yang Hao, Son petitioned for the emperor's own judgment, urging encouragement and reassurance so that the campaign might be brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 又應泰曾以築城之議為鎬罪案，謂堅城得志，啟朝鮮異日之患，於是昖奏辨。

translations.literal: Moreover Ding Yingtai had made fortification a charge against Yang Hao, holding that if strong walls were built the invaders would grow bold and sow future trouble for Korea; Son thereupon submitted a memorial in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ding Yingtai had made fortification a charge against Yang Hao, holding that if strong walls were built the invaders would grow bold and sow future trouble for Korea; Son thereupon submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「連年用兵發餉，以爾國素效忠順故也，毋以人言自疑。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We have raised troops and disbursed rations year after year because your country has always shown loyalty and obedience; do not let others' words make you doubt yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "We have raised troops and disbursed rations year after year because your country has always shown loyalty and obedience; do not let others' words make you doubt yourselves."

sentences.zh: 九月，將士分道進兵，劉綎進逼行長營，約行長為好會。

translations.literal: In the ninth month officers and soldiers advanced by separate routes; Liu Ting pressed toward Yukinaga's camp and arranged a friendly meeting with Yukinaga.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month officers and soldiers advanced by separate routes; Liu Ting pressed toward Yukinaga's camp and arranged a friendly meeting with him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，攻城，斬首九十二。

translations.literal: The next day they assaulted the city and beheaded ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they assaulted the city and beheaded ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 陳璘舟師協堵擊，毀倭船百餘。

translations.literal: Chen Lin's fleet coordinated in a blockading attack and destroyed more than a hundred Japanese ships.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lin's fleet coordinated in a blockading attack and destroyed more than a hundred Japanese ships.

sentences.zh: 行長潛出千餘騎扼之，綎不利，退，璘亦棄舟走。

translations.literal: Yukinaga secretly sent out more than a thousand cavalry to block him; Liu Ting fared badly and withdrew, and Chen Lin also abandoned his ships and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yukinaga secretly sent out more than a thousand cavalry to block him; Liu Ting fared badly and withdrew, and Chen Lin also abandoned his ships and fled.

sentences.zh: 麻貴至蔚山，頗有斬獲，倭偽退誘之。

translations.literal: Ma Gui reached Ulsan and had considerable kills and captures; the Japanese feigned retreat to lure him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui reached Ulsan and had considerable kills and captures; the Japanese feigned retreat to lure him.

sentences.zh: 貴入空壘，伏兵起，遂敗。

translations.literal: Ma Gui entered the empty fortress; ambush troops rose up, and he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui entered the empty fortress; ambush troops rose up, and he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 董一元進取晉州，乘勝渡江，連毀二寨。

translations.literal: Dong Yiyuan advanced to take Jinju, crossed the river on the momentum of victory, and destroyed two stockades in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yiyuan advanced to take Jinju, crossed the river on the momentum of victory, and destroyed two stockades in succession.

sentences.zh: 倭退保泗州老營，鏖戰下之，前逼新寨。

translations.literal: The Japanese fell back to hold the old camp at Sacheon; after fierce fighting it was taken, and the army pressed forward toward the new stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese fell back to hold the old camp at Sacheon; after fierce fighting the Ming forces took it and pressed forward toward the new stockade.

sentences.zh: 寨三面臨江，一面通陸，引海為濠，海艘泊寨下千計，築金海、固城為左右翼。

translations.literal: The stockade faced the river on three sides and connected to land on one; seawater was drawn in as a moat; more than a thousand sea vessels moored beneath the stockade; Jinhae and Goseong were built as wings on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade faced the river on three sides and connected to land on one; seawater was drawn in as a moat; more than a thousand sea vessels moored beneath it; Jinhae and Goseong were built as wings on left and right.

sentences.zh: 十月，董一元遣將四面攻城，用火器擊碎寨門，兵競前拔柵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Dong Yiyuan dispatched generals to assault the city from all four sides; using firearms they smashed the stockade gate, and the troops competed to advance and seize the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Dong Yiyuan dispatched generals to assault the city from all four sides; using firearms they smashed the stockade gate, and the troops vied to advance and seize the palisades.

sentences.zh: 忽營中火藥崩，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: Suddenly in the camp gunpowder exploded; smoke and flames filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly gunpowder in the camp detonated, and smoke and flames rose to fill the sky.

sentences.zh: 倭乘勢衝擊，固城倭亦至，兵遂大潰，奔還晉州。

translations.literal: The Japanese seized the momentum and charged; Japanese from Goseong also arrived; the army was utterly routed and fled back to Jinju.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese seized the moment and charged; Japanese from Goseong also arrived, and the army broke in complete rout, fleeing back to Jinju.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，命斬二遊擊以徇，一元等各帶罪立功。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and ordered two Mobile Corps commanders beheaded as a warning; Dong Yiyuan and the others were each ordered to redeem their crimes through meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered two guerrilla commanders beheaded as a warning to the army; Dong Yiyuan and the others were each told to redeem their offenses by winning merit in battle.

sentences.zh: 是月，福建都御史金學曾報七月九日平秀吉死，各倭俱有歸志。

translations.literal: That month Fujian Censor-in-Chief Jin Xueceng reported that Hideyoshi died on the ninth day of the seventh month in Japan, and all the Japanese wished to return home.
translations.idiomatic: That month Fujian Censor-in-Chief Jin Xueceng reported that Hideyoshi had died in Japan on the ninth day of the seventh month, and the Japanese forces all wished to go home.

sentences.zh: 十一月，清正發舟先走，麻貴遂入島山、酉浦，劉綎攻奪曳橋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Kiyomasa launched boats and fled first; Ma Gui then entered Sanchon and Yuro; Liu Ting attacked and seized Yegeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kiyomasa put to sea and fled first; Ma Gui then entered Sanchon and Yuro, and Liu Ting attacked and took Yegeo.

sentences.zh: 石曼子引舟師救行長，陳璘邀擊敗之。

translations.literal: Shimazu led a naval force to rescue Yukinaga; Chen Lin intercepted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shimazu led a fleet to relieve Yukinaga, but Chen Lin intercepted him and won the battle.

sentences.zh: 諸倭揚帆盡歸。

translations.literal: All the Japanese hoisted sails and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese hoisted sail and departed for home.

sentences.zh: 自倭亂朝鮮七載，喪師數十萬，糜餉數百萬，中朝與屬國迄無勝算，至關白死而禍始息。

translations.literal: From the time the Japanese ravaged Korea for seven years, hundreds of thousands of troops were lost and millions in military pay squandered; the Central Court and its tributary state never had a sure prospect of victory—only when the kampaku died did the calamity begin to subside.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years the Japanese had ravaged Korea; hundreds of thousands of soldiers had been lost and millions in rations wasted, and neither the Central Court nor its tributary kingdom had ever held a clear prospect of victory—only with the kampaku's death did the disaster begin to ebb.

sentences.zh: 二十七年閏四月，以平倭詔告天下，又敕諭昖曰：「倭奴平秀吉肆為不道，蹂躪爾邦。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the twenty-seventh year an edict announcing the pacification of the Japanese was proclaimed throughout the empire; also an imperial command instructed Son, saying: "The Japanese slave Hideyoshi has unrestrainedly acted against the Way and trampled your state.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of the twenty-seventh year an edict announcing the defeat of the Japanese was proclaimed throughout the empire, and an imperial command was sent to Son, saying: "The Japanese warlord Hideyoshi has wantonly violated all propriety and trampled your kingdom.

sentences.zh: 朕念王世篤忠貞，深用憫惻。

translations.literal: We consider Your Majesty's house deeply loyal and steadfast, and are profoundly moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: We have long regarded your royal house as deeply loyal and steadfast, and Our heart is full of compassion for you.

sentences.zh: 七年之中，日以此賊為事。

translations.literal: For seven years, day after day We have had this bandit as Our concern.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years this enemy has been Our daily preoccupation.

sentences.zh: 始行薄伐，繼示包容，終加嚴討。

translations.literal: At first We launched a limited punitive expedition; then showed forbearance; finally imposed severe chastisement.
translations.idiomatic: At first We sent a limited punitive force; then showed forbearance; at last We brought down stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 蓋不殺乃天之心，而用兵非予得已。

translations.literal: For sparing life is Heaven's intent, yet to employ the army was not something We could avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's heart is to spare life, yet to take up arms was not a course We could refuse.

sentences.zh: 安疆靖亂，宜取蕩平。

translations.literal: To secure the frontier and quell disorder, complete pacification was the fitting course.
translations.idiomatic: To secure the borders and still the turmoil, nothing less than total pacification would suffice.

sentences.zh: 神惡凶盈，陰殲魁首，大師乘之，追奔逐北，鯨鯢盡戮，海隅載清，捷書來聞，憂勞始釋。

translations.literal: The spirits loathe overflowing wickedness; Heaven silently destroyed the ringleader; Our great army seized the opportunity, pursued the fleeing foe, slaughtered the monsters entirely, cleared the coastal regions, and when the victory dispatch arrived, Our cares began to lift.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits abhor overflowing evil; Heaven secretly destroyed the chief culprit; Our great army seized the moment, pursued the fleeing enemy, and cut down the monsters to the last; the coastlands were cleared at last, and when the victory report arrived, Our long anxiety began to lift.

sentences.zh: 惟王雖還舊物，實同新造，振凋起敝，為力倍艱。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has recovered your former possessions, it is in truth like building anew; to revive the withered and raise up the ruined will require redoubled effort.
translations.idiomatic: Though you have recovered what was yours, it is in truth like beginning again; to revive what is withered and rebuild what is broken will demand twice the strength.

sentences.zh: 倭雖遁歸，族類尚在。

translations.literal: Though the Japanese have fled home, their kind still remain.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Japanese have withdrawn, their people still endure across the sea.

sentences.zh: 茲命邢玠振旅歸京，量留萬世德等分佈戍守。

translations.literal: We now order Xing Jie to withdraw the army and return to the capital, leaving Wan Shide and others in measured numbers to distribute garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: We now order Xing Jie to withdraw the army and return to the capital, leaving Wan Shide and others behind in appropriate numbers to garrison and defend.

sentences.zh: 王宜臥薪嚐膽，無忘前恥，惟忠惟孝，纘紹前休。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, never forgetting former shame; with loyalty and filial piety, continue the former glory."
translations.idiomatic: You must sleep on brushwood and taste gall, never forgetting the humiliations of the past; with loyalty and filial devotion, carry forward the glory of your forebears."

sentences.zh: 五月，玠條陳東征善後事宜十事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jie submitted in detail ten items concerning post-campaign arrangements for the eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xing Jie submitted a detailed list of ten items on postwar arrangements for the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 一，留戍兵，馬步水陸共計三萬四千有奇，馬三千匹。

translations.literal: First, retain garrison troops: cavalry, infantry, and naval forces by land and sea totaling more than thirty-four thousand, with three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: First, retain garrison troops—cavalry, infantry, and naval forces by land and sea totaling more than thirty-four thousand men, with three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 一，定月餉，每年計銀九十一萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Second, fix monthly rations: each year totaling more than nine hundred eighteen thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Second, fix monthly pay: more than nine hundred eighteen thousand taels of silver per year.

sentences.zh: 一，定本色，合用米豆，分派遼東、天津、山東等處，每年十三萬石。

translations.literal: Third, fix grain rations in kind: rice and beans to be supplied from Liaodong, Tianjin, Shandong, and other places, one hundred thirty thousand shi each year.
translations.idiomatic: Third, fix grain rations in kind: rice and beans to be allocated from Liaodong, Tianjin, Shandong, and elsewhere, totaling one hundred thirty thousand shi per year.

sentences.zh: 一，留中路海防道。

translations.literal: Fourth, retain the Central Route Coastal Defense Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, retain the Central Route Coastal Defense Intendant.

sentences.zh: 一，裁餉司。

translations.literal: Fifth, establish a rations office.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, establish a rations office.

sentences.zh: 一，重將領。

translations.literal: Sixth, give weight to commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, strengthen the authority of field commanders.

sentences.zh: 一，添巡捕。

translations.literal: Seventh, add patrol and arrest forces.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, add patrol and pursuit units.

sentences.zh: 一，分汛地。

translations.literal: Eighth, divide sectors of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, divide coastal defense sectors.

sentences.zh: 一，議操練。

translations.literal: Ninth, discuss drill and training.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, institute drill and training.

sentences.zh: 一，責成本國。

translations.literal: Tenth, hold the host country responsible for costs.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, hold Korea itself responsible for the costs.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議：「數年疲耗，今始息肩，自宜內固根本，不當更為繁費。

translations.literal: Court officials deliberated: "For years resources have been drained; now at last there is relief from the burden; naturally the interior should be fortified at its foundations, and further heavy expenditure should not be made.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued: "For years the empire has been drained; now at last the burden is lifting. We ought to strengthen our foundations at home, not incur further heavy costs.

sentences.zh: 況彼國兵荒之後，不獨苦倭之擾，兼苦我兵。

translations.literal: Moreover that country, after war and famine, suffers not only from Japanese harassment but also from hardship caused by our troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after war and famine that country suffers not only from Japanese raids but also from the burden of our own troops.

sentences.zh: 故今日善後事宜，仍當商之彼國，先量彼餉之贏絀，始可酌我兵之去留。

translations.literal: Therefore today's postwar arrangements should still be discussed with that country; first measure whether their rations are surplus or deficient, and only then determine whether our troops should stay or withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Postwar arrangements should therefore be negotiated with Korea first: only after gauging whether their supplies are adequate can we decide how many of our troops to keep or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 至於增買馬匹，添補標兵，創立巡捕，及至管餉府佐，悉宜停止。」

translations.literal: As for increasing horse purchases, adding standard troops, establishing patrol forces, and even the rations-office assistants, all should be halted."
translations.idiomatic: As for buying more horses, adding standard troops, creating new patrol units, and even the rations-office assistants—all of that should be stopped."

sentences.zh: 帝命督撫會同國王酌奏。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the grand coordinators to consult with the king and submit considered recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the grand coordinators to consult with the king and submit a considered plan.

sentences.zh: 八月，昖獻方物，助大工，褒賞如例。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Son presented local products to assist the great construction project, and was rewarded according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Son sent tribute goods to assist the great palace works and received rewards according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 十月，請留水兵八千，以資戍守。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he requested that eight thousand naval troops be retained to support garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he asked that eight thousand naval troops be kept behind to help with coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 其撤回官兵，駐劄遼陽備警。

translations.literal: The withdrawn officers and soldiers were stationed at Liaoyang on alert.
translations.idiomatic: The troops being withdrawn were stationed at Liaoyang to stand watch.

sentences.zh: 二十八年四月請將義州等倉遺下米豆運回遼陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year he requested that the rice and beans left in storehouses at Uiju and elsewhere be transported back to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year he asked that the rice and beans left in storehouses at Uiju and elsewhere be shipped back to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 戶部議：「輸運維艱，莫若徑與彼國，振其雕敝，以昭皇仁。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated: "Transport is difficult; better to give it directly to that country, revive its exhausted state, and display imperial benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue argued: "Transport is too difficult; better to give the grain directly to Korea, revive its devastated land, and display the emperor's benevolence."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Let it be so."

sentences.zh: 二十九年二月，兵部覆奏經督條陳七事：「一，練兵士。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of War submitted in reply seven items proposed by the grand coordinator: "First, drill the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of War replied with seven proposals from the grand coordinator: "First, drill the troops.

sentences.zh: 麗人鷙悍耐寒苦，而長衫大袖，訓練無方，宜以束伍之法教之。

translations.literal: Korean men are fierce and hardy, enduring cold and hardship, yet wear long gowns with wide sleeves and are trained without method; they should be taught by the method of binding squads into units.
translations.idiomatic: Koreans are fierce and hardy, able to endure cold and hardship, yet they wear long gowns with wide sleeves and are drilled without discipline; they should be taught proper squad organization and formation.

sentences.zh: 一，守沖要。

translations.literal: Second, hold strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Second, hold the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮三面距海，釜山與對馬相望，巨濟次之，宜各守以重兵，並蔚山、開山等處皆宜戍守。

translations.literal: Korea is bounded by sea on three sides; Busan faces Tsushima across the water, Geoje is next in importance; each should be held with heavy forces, and Ulsan, Gaesan, and other places should also be garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Korea is bounded by sea on three sides; Busan faces Tsushima across the strait, with Geoje next in importance—each should be held by strong garrisons, and Ulsan, Gaesan, and other points should be defended as well.

sentences.zh: 一，修險隘。

translations.literal: Third, repair strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Third, repair the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 王京北倚叢山，南環滄海。

translations.literal: The royal capital leans on clustered mountains to the north and is encircled by the blue sea to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The capital rests against mountains to the north and is ringed by the sea to the south.

sentences.zh: 忠州左右烏、竹二嶺，羊腸繞曲，有一夫當關之險。

translations.literal: To the left and right of Chungju are the two ridges of U and Juk; the paths wind like sheep intestines, with the peril of one man holding the pass.
translations.idiomatic: To either side of Chungju lie the U and Juk ridges, where the paths twist like sheep intestines and a single man can hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 今營壘遺址尚存，亟宜修葺。

translations.literal: The sites of former camps and fortifications still remain; they should urgently be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: The ruins of old camps and fortifications still stand; they should be repaired at once.

sentences.zh: 一，建城池。

translations.literal: Fourth, build city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, build fortified cities.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮八道，十九無城。

translations.literal: Of Korea's eight provinces, nine-tenths have no walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: Of Korea's eight provinces, nine in ten have no walled cities.

sentences.zh: 平壤西北鴨、浿二江，俱南通海。

translations.literal: Northwest of Pyongyang the Yalu and Taedong rivers both reach the sea to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Pyongyang the Yalu and Taedong rivers both run south to the sea.

sentences.zh: 倘倭別遣一旅佔據平壤，則王京聲援斷絕，皆應修築屯聚。

translations.literal: If the Japanese should send a separate detachment to occupy Pyongyang, contact with the royal capital would be cut off; all these places should be fortified and garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: If the Japanese were to send a separate force to seize Pyongyang, the capital would be cut off from support; all these places should be fortified and held.

sentences.zh: 一，造器械。

translations.literal: Fifth, manufacture weapons and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, manufacture arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 倭戰便陸不便海，以船制重大，不利攻擊。

translations.literal: The Japanese fight well on land but not at sea, because their ships are large and heavy and ill suited to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese fight well on land but poorly at sea, for their ships are large and heavy and poorly suited to offensive action.

sentences.zh: 今准福唬造百十艘為奇兵，並添造神機百子火箭。

translations.literal: Now permit the construction of one hundred-odd Fujian-style ships as a flank force, and additionally manufacture divine-engine hundred-bolt rockets.
translations.idiomatic: Authorize the building of one hundred-odd Fujian-style warships as a surprise force, along with additional divine-engine hundred-bolt rockets.

sentences.zh: 一，訪異材。

translations.literal: Sixth, seek out exceptional talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, seek out men of exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮貴世官，賊世役，一切禁錮，往往走倭走敵，為本國患，宜破格搜采。

translations.literal: Korea honors hereditary office and despises hereditary service; all are confined by status, and many flee to the Japanese or to the enemy, becoming a plague on their own country; exceptional men should be sought without regard to convention.
translations.idiomatic: Korea honors hereditary office and despises hereditary service; talent is locked in by status, and many flee to the Japanese or to the enemy, becoming a scourge at home—men of ability should be sought without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 一，修內治。

translations.literal: Seventh, improve internal governance.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, strengthen internal governance.

sentences.zh: 國家東南臨海，以登、旅為門戶，鎮江為咽喉，應援之兵，不宜盡撤。

translations.literal: Our state faces the sea to the southeast; Dengzhou and Lüshun are the gateway, Zhenjiang the throat; the troops held in reserve for reinforcement should not all be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Our empire faces the sea to the southeast; Dengzhou and Lüshun are its gateway and Zhenjiang its throat—the troops held in reserve for reinforcement should not all be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 我自固，亦所以固朝鮮也。」

translations.literal: By securing ourselves we also secure Korea."
translations.idiomatic: By securing ourselves we also secure Korea."

sentences.zh: 詔朝鮮刻勵以行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Korea to implement these measures with earnest effort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Korea to carry out these measures with all diligence.

sentences.zh: 九月，奏所頒誥命冕服遭變淪失，祈補給，從之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month a memorial reported that the patents of investiture and ceremonial robes previously granted had been lost in the upheaval, and requested replacements; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month a memorial reported that the patents of investiture and ceremonial robes previously granted had been lost in the war and asked for replacements; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 時倭國內亂，對馬島主平義智悉遣降人還朝鮮，遺書乞和，且揚言秀吉將家康將輸糧數十萬石為軍興資，以脅朝鮮。

translations.literal: At that time Japan was torn by internal disorder; Yoshitoshi, lord of Tsushima Island, sent all the surrendered men back to Korea with a letter begging peace, and also spread word that Hideyoshi's heir Ieyasu would supply several hundred thousand shi of grain as funds for raising troops, to coerce Korea.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Japan was torn by civil strife; Yoshitoshi, lord of Tsushima, sent all surrendered men back to Korea with a letter suing for peace, and also spread word that Ieyasu, Hideyoshi's heir, would supply several hundred thousand shi of grain to finance an army—aimed at coercing Korea.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮與對馬島一水相望，島地不產五穀，資米於朝鮮。

translations.literal: Korea and Tsushima Island are separated by only a strip of water; the island produces no grain and relies on Korea for rice.
translations.idiomatic: Korea and Tsushima are separated by only a narrow strait; the island grows no grain and depends on Korea for rice.

sentences.zh: 兵興後，絕開市，因百計脅款。

translations.literal: After the war began, trade was cut off; therefore they used every stratagem to coerce a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: After the war began trade was cut off, and they resorted to every stratagem to force a settlement.

sentences.zh: 秀吉死，我軍盡撤，朝鮮畏倭滋甚。

translations.literal: When Hideyoshi died and our army was fully withdrawn, Korea's fear of the Japanese grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Hideyoshi died and our troops were fully withdrawn, Korea's fear of the Japanese only grew.

sentences.zh: 欲與倭通款，又懼開罪中國。

translations.literal: They wished to treat with the Japanese, yet feared offending China.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to treat with the Japanese, yet feared offending the Ming court.

sentences.zh: 十二月，昖以島倭求款來請命。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Son came to request instructions because the island Japanese sought a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Son petitioned for guidance because the island Japanese were seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 兵部以事難遙度，令總督世德酌議，詔可。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War held that the matter was hard to judge from afar and ordered Grand Coordinator Shide to deliberate; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War held that the matter could not be judged from afar and ordered Grand Coordinator Wan Shide to decide as he saw fit; an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 三十年十一月，昖言倭使頻來要脅和款，兵端漸露，乞選將率兵，督同本國訓練修防。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirtieth year Son reported that Japanese envoys came repeatedly to coerce a settlement, signs of renewed hostilities were appearing, and he begged that generals be chosen to lead troops and supervise training and defense together with his country.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirtieth year Son reported that Japanese envoys kept coming to demand peace on their terms, signs of renewed fighting were appearing, and he asked that generals be sent to lead troops and oversee training and defense alongside his own forces.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「曾留將士教習，成法具在，無容再遣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Officers and soldiers were once left behind to instruct and drill; the established methods are all in place; there is no need to send more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Officers and soldiers were already left behind to train your forces; the established methods are all in place—there is no need to send more.

sentences.zh: 因命其使臣齎敕誡勵。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Son's envoys to carry an imperial command of admonition and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Son's envoys to carry back an imperial command of admonition and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 三十三年九月，昖復請封琿為世子，禮部仍執立長之議。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-third year Son again requested that Hun be enfeoffed as heir apparent; the Ministry of Rites still held to the principle of establishing the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-third year Son again asked that Hun be invested as heir apparent; the Ministry of Rites still insisted on the principle of favoring the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 三十五年四月，昖以家康求和來告，兵部議聽王自計而已。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-fifth year Son reported that Ieyasu sought peace; the Ministry of War deliberated that the king should decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirty-fifth year Son reported that Ieyasu was seeking peace; the Ministry of War decided to leave the decision to the king.

sentences.zh: 由是和款不絕，後三年始畫開市之事。

translations.literal: Thus peace negotiations continued without cease; only three years later were arrangements for reopening trade finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Peace negotiations continued without interruption, and only three years later were terms for reopening trade finally settled.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，昖卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year Son died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year Son died.

sentences.zh: 光海君琿自稱署國事，追陪臣來訃，且請諡。

translations.literal: Gwanghae-gun Hun styled himself as administering state affairs, sent attending ministers in pursuit to announce the death, and also requested a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Gwanghae-gun Hun proclaimed himself regent, sent court ministers posthaste to announce the death, and also requested a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其擅，不允，令該國臣民公義以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked his presumption and did not consent, ordering that the officials and people of that country reach a public decision and report it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disliked his presumption and refused; he ordered the officials and people of Korea to reach a public decision and report back.

sentences.zh: 時我大清兵征服各部，漸近朝鮮。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Our Great Qing were conquering the various tribes and gradually drawing near Korea.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies of the rising Qing were subduing the Jurchen tribes one by one and drawing ever closer to Korea.

sentences.zh: 兵部議令該王大修武備，整飭邊防，並請敕遼左督撫鎮臣，遣官宣達毋相侵犯之意。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated that the king of that country should greatly strengthen military preparations and put the frontier defenses in order, and also requested an edict to the grand coordinators and garrison commanders of eastern Liaodong to dispatch officials proclaiming the intent not to violate one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War proposed that the Korean king greatly strengthen his defenses and put the frontier in order, and also asked that an edict be sent to the grand coordinators and garrison commanders of Liaodong to dispatch envoys proclaiming the intent of mutual non-aggression.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 十月，封琿為國王，從其臣民請也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Hun was enfeoffed as king, in accordance with the request of his officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Hun was invested as king, at the request of his officials and people.

sentences.zh: 三十七年二月，諡昖曰昭敬，遣官賜琿及妃柳氏誥命。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-seventh year Son was given the posthumous title Zhaojing; officials were dispatched to bestow patents of investiture on Hun and his consort Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-seventh year Son was given the posthumous title Zhaojing; envoys were dispatched to bestow patents of investiture on Hun and his consort, Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 初，朝鮮失守，賴中國力得復，倭棄釜山遁。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Korea lost its defenses, it recovered only through China's strength; the Japanese abandoned Busan and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Korea's defenses collapsed, it recovered only through Ming power; the Japanese abandoned Busan and fled.

sentences.zh: 然陰謀啟疆，為患不已。

translations.literal: Yet they secretly plotted territorial expansion, and the trouble did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they secretly plotted to expand their territory, and the threat never ceased.

sentences.zh: 於是海上流言倭圖釜山，朝鮮與之通。

translations.literal: Thereupon rumors spread at sea that the Japanese intended Busan and that Korea was in communication with them.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread along the coast that the Japanese were plotting against Busan and that Korea was in secret communication with them.

sentences.zh: 四十一年九月，總兵官楊宗業以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-first year Regional Commander Yang Zongye reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-first year Regional Commander Yang Zongye reported the rumors to the court.

sentences.zh: 琿疏辨，詔慰解之。

translations.literal: Hun submitted a memorial in his own defense; an edict comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun submitted a memorial in his own defense; an edict comforted him and set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 四十二年四月，奏請追封生母金氏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the forty-second year he memorialized requesting posthumous enfeoffment for his birth mother, the Lady Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the forty-second year he memorialized asking that his birth mother, Lady Jin, be granted posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 禮部按《會典》，嫡母受封而生母先亡者得追贈，乃命封為國王次妃。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites consulted the Collected Statutes: when the principal wife received enfeoffment and the birth mother had already died, posthumous bestowal was permitted; he was therefore ordered enfeoffed as the king's secondary consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites consulted the Collected Statutes, which held that when the principal wife had been enfeoffed and the birth mother was already dead, posthumous honors could be granted; Lady Jin was therefore enfeoffed as the king's secondary consort.

sentences.zh: 四十三年十一月，表賀冬至，因奏買回《吾學編》、《弇山堂別集》等書，載本國事與《會典》乖錯，乞改正。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the forty-third year he submitted a felicitations table for the winter solstice and also memorialized that he had bought back books such as Wuxue Bian and Yanshan Tang Bieji, which recorded affairs of his country in ways that conflicted with the Collected Statutes, and begged that they be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the forty-third year he sent felicitations for the winter solstice and also reported that he had bought back books such as Wuxue Bian and Yanshan Tang Bieji, whose accounts of Korean affairs conflicted with the Collected Statutes, and asked that the errors be corrected.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「野史不足憑。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Unofficial histories are not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied: "Unofficial histories are not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 今所請恥與逆黨同譏，宜憫其誠，宣付史館。」

translations.literal: What is now requested shows shame at being mocked together with rebellious factions; his sincerity should be pitied, and the matter should be announced to the Historiography Institute."
translations.idiomatic: What he asks shows his shame at being mocked alongside rebellious factions; his sincerity deserves compassion, and the matter should be referred to the Historiography Institute."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The reply approved.

sentences.zh: 初，琿為生母已得封，至是復祈給冠服。

translations.literal: Earlier Hun had already obtained enfeoffment for his birth mother; now he again petitioned for the grant of ceremonial cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Hun had already secured enfeoffment for his birth mother; now he petitioned again for the grant of ceremonial cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 禮臣以金氏側室，禮有隆殺，執不可。

translations.literal: Rites officials held that the Lady Jin was a secondary consort and that ritual had gradations of honor and abasement; they steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials held that Lady Jin was a secondary consort and that ritual distinctions of rank forbade it; they steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 四十五年正月，琿請至再，帝以琿屢次懇陳，勉從之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-fifth year Hun petitioned again and again; the emperor, because Hun had repeatedly pleaded earnestly, reluctantly consented.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-fifth year Hun petitioned again and again; the emperor, moved by his repeated earnest pleas, reluctantly consented.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，楊鎬督馬林、杜松、劉綎等出師，為我大清兵所敗。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Yang Hao supervised Ma Lin, Du Song, Liu Ting, and others in taking the field; they were defeated by the armies of Our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year Yang Hao led Ma Lin, Du Song, Liu Ting, and others into the field; they were defeated by the Qing armies.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮助戰兵將，或降或戰死。

translations.literal: Among the Korean officers and soldiers who aided in the fighting, some surrendered and some died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Korean officers and soldiers who fought alongside them, some surrendered and some died in battle.

sentences.zh: 琿告急，詔加優恤。

translations.literal: Hun reported an emergency; an edict granted extra favor and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Hun sent an urgent appeal for aid; the court responded with an edict granting him special favor and relief.

sentences.zh: 十一月，兵部覆：朝鮮入貢之道，宜添兵防守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Ministry of War replied: The route by which Korea comes to offer tribute should have troops added to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Ministry of War replied that the route by which Korean tribute envoys traveled ought to be reinforced with additional garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 詔鎮江等處設兵將，令經略熊廷弼調委。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that commanders and troops be established at Jiang and other places, to be dispatched under the coordination of Grand Coordinator Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that commanders and troops be posted at Jiang and other strategic points, to be assigned and coordinated by Grand Coordinator Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 四十八年正月，琿奏：「敵兵八月中攻破北關，金台吉自焚，白羊出降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-eighth year, Hun memorialized: "In the eighth month the enemy broke through the North Pass; Jin Taiji burned himself, and Bai Yang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-eighth year Hun memorialized: "In the eighth month the enemy broke through the North Pass; Jin Taiji burned himself to death, and Bai Yang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 鐵嶺之役，蒙古宰賽亦為所滅。

translations.literal: In the Battle of Tieling, the Mongol Zaisai was also destroyed by them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Tieling the Mongol chieftain Zaisai was destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 聞其國謀議以朝鮮、北關、宰賽皆助兵南朝，今北關、宰賽皆滅，不可使朝鮮獨存。

translations.literal: It is heard that in their country they deliberate that Korea, the North Pass, and Zaisai all sent troops to aid the Southern Dynasty; now that the North Pass and Zaisai are both destroyed, Korea must not be left standing alone.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that in their councils they argue that Korea, the North Pass, and Zaisai all sent troops to aid the Ming; now that the North Pass and Zaisai are both destroyed, Korea must not be allowed to survive alone.

sentences.zh: 又聞設兵牛毛寨、萬遮嶺，欲略寬奠、鎮江等處。

translations.literal: It is also heard that they have stationed troops at Niumao Stockade and Wanzhe Ridge, intending to raid Kuandian, Jiang, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: We also hear that they have posted troops at Niumao Stockade and Wanzhe Ridge, intending to raid Kuandian, Jiang, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 寬奠、鎮江與昌城、義州諸堡隔水相望，孤危非常。

translations.literal: Kuandian, Jiang, and the forts of Changcheng, Uiju, and the like face one another across the water; they are extremely isolated and perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Kuandian, Jiang, and the forts at Changcheng, Uiju, and elsewhere stand isolated on opposite banks of the river, exposed to extraordinary danger.

sentences.zh: 敵若從靉陽境上鴉鶻關取路繞出鳳凰城裏，一日長驅，寬鎮、昌城俱莫自保。

translations.literal: If the enemy takes the route through Yagu Pass in the Aiyang border district and loops around inside Phoenix City, in a single day's swift advance neither Kuandian-Jiang nor Changcheng could protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy passes through Yagu Pass on the Aiyang frontier and swings around behind Phoenix City, a single day's march would leave Kuandian, Jiang, and Changcheng unable to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 內而遼左八站，外而東江一城，彼此隔斷，聲援阻絕，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Within, the Eight Stations of eastern Liaodong; without, the single city of the Eastern River—they are severed from one another, mutual support blocked; it is enough to chill the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Within lie the Eight Stations of eastern Liaodong; without stands the lone city of the Eastern River garrison—they would be cut off from one another, mutual aid impossible. The prospect is enough to chill the heart.

sentences.zh: 望速調大兵，共為掎角，以固邊防。」

translations.literal: We hope great troops will be rapidly dispatched, together forming pincers, to secure the frontier defenses."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that large reinforcements be sent at once so that our forces may act in concert as pincers and hold the frontier firm."

sentences.zh: 時遼鎮塘報稱朝鮮與大清講和，朝議遂謂琿陽衡陰順，宜遣官宣諭，或命將監護，其說紛拿。

translations.literal: At that time urgent reports from the Liaodong garrison said Korea had made peace with the Great Qing; court opinion then held that Hun was openly resistant but secretly compliant, and that an official should be sent to proclaim instructions, or a general ordered to supervise and protect—the views were tangled and disputed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time urgent reports from the Liaodong garrison claimed that Korea had made peace with the Qing. Court opinion then held that Hun was defiant in public but colluding in secret, and that an envoy should be sent to instruct him—or a general appointed to supervise him. The proposals were tangled and hotly disputed.

sentences.zh: 琿疏辨：「二百年忠誠事大，死生一節。」

translations.literal: Hun submitted a memorial in his own defense: "Two hundred years of loyal service to the great power, one steadfast principle in life and death."
translations.idiomatic: Hun submitted a memorial in his own defense: "For two hundred years we have served the great power with loyal devotion, holding one and the same principle in life and death."

sentences.zh: 詞極剴摯。

translations.literal: The language was extremely earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The language was profoundly earnest and moving.

sentences.zh: 禮、兵二部請降敕令曉諭，以安其心。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Rites and War requested that an edict be issued for proclamation, to put his mind at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Rites and War asked that an edict be issued to reassure him and settle his mind.

sentences.zh: 帝是其議，然敕令陪臣往，不遣官也。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their proposal, but the edict was sent through envoys from his court, and no Ming official was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved their proposal, but the edict was conveyed through Korean envoys; no Ming official was sent.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年八月，改朝鮮貢道，自海至登州，直達京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianqi, Korea's tribute route was changed—from sea to Dengzhou, then directly to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianqi the Korean tribute route was changed: envoys would travel by sea to Dengzhou and then proceed directly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時毛文龍以總兵鎮皮島，招集逃民為兵，而仰給於朝鮮。

translations.literal: At that time Mao Wenlong as regional commander garrisoned Pidao, gathering fugitive commoners as soldiers and relying on Korea for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Regional Commander Mao Wenlong held Pidao, recruiting fugitives as soldiers and depending on Korea for supplies.

sentences.zh: 十一月，琿奏力難饋餉，乞循萬曆東征例，發運山東粟，從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Hun memorialized that he could scarcely sustain supplies, and begged that the precedent of the Wanli eastern expedition be followed to dispatch grain from Shandong; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hun memorialized that he could scarcely keep up the supply effort and asked that grain be shipped from Shandong as in the Wanli eastern expedition; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，國人廢琿而立其侄綾陽君倧，以昭敬王妃之命權國事，令議政府移文督撫轉奏，文龍為之揭報。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, the people deposed Hun and installed his nephew Lingyang Lord Jeong, who under orders from Queen Dowager Zhaojing provisionally handled state affairs; the State Council was ordered to send a dispatch to the grand coordinators for relayed report; Mao Wenlong submitted a bulletin on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year the people deposed Hun and enthroned his nephew Lingyang Lord Jeong, who under Queen Dowager Zhaojing's authority provisionally governed the realm. The State Council was instructed to notify the grand coordinators through official correspondence, and Mao Wenlong reported the matter in a bulletin.

sentences.zh: 登州巡撫袁可立上言：「琿果不道，宜聽太妃具奏，以待中國更立。」

translations.literal: Dengzhou Grand Coordinator Yuan Keli submitted: "If Hun is indeed immoral, the queen dowager should be allowed to memorialize fully, to await China's re-installation of a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou Grand Coordinator Yuan Keli submitted: "If Hun has truly acted wickedly, the queen dowager should be allowed to memorialize in full and await the Ming court's decision on who should reign."

sentences.zh: 疏留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was held at court without action.

sentences.zh: 八月，王妃金氏疏請封倧，禮部尚書林堯俞言：「朝鮮廢立之事，內外諸臣抒忠發憤，有謂宜聲罪致討者，有謂勿遽討且受方貢核顛末者，或謂當責以大義，察輿情之向背者，或謂當令亻宗討敵自洗者，眾論鹹有可采。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Queen Dowager Lady Jin submitted a memorial requesting Jeong be enfeoffed. Minister of Rites Lin Yaoyu said: "In the matter of Korea's deposition and installation, officials within and without have expressed loyal indignation: Some say one should proclaim guilt and launch punitive action; some say one should not hasten to attack but should accept their tribute missions and verify the facts; some say one should charge them with the great principle and observe the drift of public sentiment; some say Jeong should be ordered to attack the enemy to clear himself—all worthy views worth considering.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Queen Dowager Lady Jin submitted a memorial asking that Jeong be invested as king. Minister of Rites Lin Yaoyu said: "On Korea's deposition and enthronement, officials inside and outside the court have spoken with loyal indignation. Some urge proclaiming guilt and launching punitive action; some urge holding off on attack, accepting their tribute missions, and verifying the facts; some urge holding them to the great principle and gauging public sentiment; some urge ordering Jeong to strike the enemy and thereby clear himself—all views worth weighing.

sentences.zh: 其謂琿實悖德，倧討叛臣以赤心奉朝廷者，惟文龍一人耳。

translations.literal: Among those who held that Hun was truly immoral and that Jeong had attacked rebel ministers with a loyal heart toward the court, Mao Wenlong alone was the one.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who held that Hun had truly betrayed his duty and that Jeong had struck down rebel ministers with a loyal heart toward the Ming, Mao Wenlong alone spoke thus.

sentences.zh: 皇上奉天討逆，扶植綱常，此正法也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, upholding Heaven in punishing rebellion and upholding moral order—this is correct law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, acting under Heaven to punish rebellion and uphold moral order—this is the proper course of justice.

sentences.zh: 毋亦念彼素稱恭順，迥異諸裔，則更遣貞士信臣，會同文龍，公集臣民，再四詢訪。

translations.literal: Yet also bearing in mind that they have long been called deferential and differ entirely from other frontier peoples, then dispatch upright trusted ministers to join Mao Wenlong, publicly assemble officials and people, and inquire repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet also bearing in mind that they have long been known for deference and stand apart from other frontier peoples, dispatch upright and trusted ministers to join Mao Wenlong, publicly assemble officials and commoners, and inquire again and again.

sentences.zh: 勘辨既明，再請聖斷。」

translations.literal: Once investigation and judgment are clear, again request the sage decision."
translations.idiomatic: Once the facts have been examined and clarified, submit the matter again for Your Majesty's judgment."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The reply approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禮部復上言：「臣前同兵部移咨登撫，並劄毛師，遣官往勘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites again submitted: "Your subject previously, together with the Ministry of War, sent dispatches to the Dengzhou grand coordinator and also wrote Commander Mao, dispatching officials to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Ministry of Rites submitted again: "Your subject previously joined the Ministry of War in sending dispatches to the Dengzhou grand coordinator and in writing Commander Mao, dispatching officials to investigate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 今據申送彼國公結十二道，自宗室至八道臣民共稱倧為恭順。

translations.literal: Now according to the twelve joint petitions sent from that country, from the royal house to the officials and people of the Eight Provinces, all together call Jeong deferential.
translations.idiomatic: We now have twelve joint petitions submitted from that country, from the royal house down to the officials and people of the Eight Provinces, all declaring Jeong deferential.

sentences.zh: 且彼之陪臣相率哀籲，謂當此危急之秋，必須君國之主。

translations.literal: Moreover, their envoys have come in succession with desperate pleas, saying that in this hour of crisis a lord of the state is essential.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their envoys have come in succession with desperate pleas, saying that in this hour of crisis the realm must have a sovereign at its head.

sentences.zh: 乞先頒敕諭，令倧統理國事，仍令發兵索賦，同文龍設伏出奇，俟漸有次第，始遣重臣往正封典。

translations.literal: We beg that an edict be first issued instructing Jeong to administer state affairs; still order that troops be sent and levies collected, together with Mao Wenlong setting ambushes and striking with surprise; wait until things gradually attain order, then dispatch a senior minister to confer proper investiture.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that an edict be issued first instructing Jeong to govern state affairs, and that he be ordered to raise troops and collect levies, coordinating with Mao Wenlong in ambush and surprise attack; once affairs gradually take proper order, a senior minister may then be sent to confer formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 庶幾字小之中，不失固圉之道。」

translations.literal: Perhaps within treating the small [state], one would not lose the way of securing the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Thus Korea could be upheld as a loyal vassal without abandoning the strategy of securing the frontier."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，封倧為國王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Jeong was enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year Jeong was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，文龍報：「朝鮮逆党李適、韓明璉等起兵昌城，直趨王京，被臣擒獲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, Wenlong reported: "The rebel faction in Korea, Li Shi, Han Minglian, and others raised troops at Changcheng and marched straight on the royal capital; they were captured by your subject.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year Wenlong reported: "The rebel faction in Korea—Li Shi, Han Minglian, and others—raised troops at Changcheng and marched straight on the royal capital; your subject captured them.

sentences.zh: 餘孽韓潤、鄭梅等竄入建州，有左議府尹義立約為內應，期今冬大舉犯朝鮮。

translations.literal: The remnant bandits Han Run, Zheng Mei, and others fled into Jianzhou; Left State Councillor Yin Yili agreed to serve as inside collaborator, planning a major attack on Korea this winter.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant rebels Han Run, Zheng Mei, and others fled into Jianzhou; Left State Councillor Yin Yili agreed to serve as an inside collaborator, planning a major invasion of Korea this winter.

sentences.zh: 臣已咨國王防守，暫移鐵山之眾就雲從島柴薪。」

translations.literal: Your subject has already consulted the king on defense, and temporarily moved the forces at Tieshan to procure firewood on Yunchong Island."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has already advised the king on defense and temporarily moved the troops at Tieshan to Yunchong Island to gather firewood."

sentences.zh: 登萊巡撫武之望奏：「毛帥自五月以來，營室於須彌，所謂雲從島是也。

translations.literal: Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Wu Zhiwang memorialized: "Commander Mao since the fifth month has built quarters at Xumi—the so-called Yunchong Island.
translations.idiomatic: Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Wu Zhiwang memorialized: "Commander Mao has since the fifth month built quarters at Xumi—what is called Yunchong Island.

sentences.zh: 今十月又徙兵民商賈以實之，而鐵山之地空矣。

translations.literal: Now in the tenth month he has again moved troops, commoners, and merchants to fill it, and the land of Tieshan is empty.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the tenth month he has again moved soldiers, civilians, and merchants there to fill it out, and Tieshan has been left empty.

sentences.zh: 故朝鮮各道疑其有逼處之嫌，甚至布兵以防禦之。

translations.literal: Therefore the various provinces of Korea suspect there is an intention of pressing too close, to the point of even deploying troops in defense against him.
translations.idiomatic: Korea's provinces therefore suspect he intends to press too close, to the point of even deploying troops in defense against him.

sentences.zh: 今鎮臣所稱李適等之叛，尹義立之內應，臣等微聞之，而未敢遽信焉。

translations.literal: What the garrison commander reports regarding Li Shi and others' rebellion and Yin Yili as inside collaborator—we have faintly heard it but dare not hastily believe.
translations.idiomatic: What the garrison commander reports about the rebellion of Li Shi and others and Yin Yili's role as inside collaborator—we have heard faint rumors but dare not believe them hastily.

sentences.zh: 信之則益重鮮人之疑，不信則恐貽後來之患。」

translations.literal: If believed, it would further deepen Korean suspicion; if not believed, we fear leaving trouble for later."
translations.idiomatic: If we believe it, Korean suspicion will only deepen; if we do not, we fear trouble for the future."

sentences.zh: 兵部言：「牽制敵國者，朝鮮也；

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said: "The one who checks the enemy state is Korea;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War said: "The force that checks the enemy state is Korea;

sentences.zh: 聯屬朝鮮者，毛鎮也；

translations.literal: the one linked to Korea is the Mao garrison;
translations.idiomatic: the force linked to Korea is the Mao garrison;

sentences.zh: 駕馭毛鎮者，登撫也。

translations.literal: the one who controls the Mao garrison is the Dengzhou grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: the official who controls the Mao garrison is the Dengzhou grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 今撫臣與鎮臣不和，以至鎮臣與屬國不和，大不利。」

translations.literal: Now the grand coordinator and garrison commander are not in harmony, to the point that the garrison commander and tributary state are not in harmony—greatly unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: Now the grand coordinator and garrison commander are at odds, to the point that the garrison commander and the tributary state are at odds as well—deeply harmful."

sentences.zh: 帝乃飭勉鎮撫同心，而韓潤、尹義立等令朝鮮自處。

translations.literal: The emperor then admonished the garrison commander and grand coordinator to be of one mind, and let Korea handle Han Run, Yin Yili, and the others on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then admonished the garrison commander and grand coordinator to act in concert, and left Han Run, Yin Yili, and the others for Korea to handle on its own.

sentences.zh: 倧又請撤遼民安插中土，兵部言：「遼人去留，文龍是視。

translations.literal: Jeong again requested that Liaodong people be withdrawn and resettled in the heartland; the Ministry of War said: "Whether Liaodong people stay or go depends on Mao Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Jeong again asked that Liaodong refugees be withdrawn and resettled in the interior; the Ministry of War said: "Whether Liaodong people stay or go depends on Mao Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 文龍一日不去，則遼人一日不離。

translations.literal: As long as Wenlong does not go, Liaodong people will not leave for a day.
translations.idiomatic: As long as Wenlong remains, the Liaodong people will not leave for a single day.

sentences.zh: 鮮人驅之入島可也，驅之離島不可也。

translations.literal: It is acceptable for Koreans to drive them onto the island; it is not acceptable to drive them off the island.
translations.idiomatic: Koreans may drive them onto the island, but they must not drive them off it.

sentences.zh: 宜令鎮臣將遼民盡刷過島，登撫刻期運糧朝鮮，量行救振，以資屯牧。」

translations.literal: The garrison commander should be ordered to move all Liaodong people across to the island; the Dengzhou grand coordinator should set a deadline to transport grain to Korea and provide relief in appropriate measure, to support garrison farming."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander should be ordered to move all Liaodong people onto the island; the Dengzhou grand coordinator should set a deadline to ship grain to Korea and provide relief as needed, to support garrison farming."

sentences.zh: 帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，倧上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year, Jeong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year Jeong submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 皇朝之於小邦，覆幬之恩，視同服內。

translations.literal: The great dynasty toward our small state—its sheltering grace treats us as within the same robe.
translations.idiomatic: The great dynasty's sheltering grace toward our small kingdom treats us as though we wore the same robe as the empire itself.

sentences.zh: 頃遭昏亂，潛通敵國，皇天震怒，降黜厥命。

translations.literal: Recently we suffered turmoil and secretly communicated with the enemy state; August Heaven was enraged and lowered dismissal from our destiny.
translations.idiomatic: We recently fell into turmoil and secretly communicated with the enemy; August Heaven was enraged and removed our former king from his throne.

sentences.zh: 臣自權署之初，不敢遑寧，即命陪臣張晚為帥，李適副之，付以國中精銳，進屯甯邊，一聽毛鎮節制，以候協剿之期。

translations.literal: From the beginning of my provisional authority I dared not rest easy; I immediately appointed envoy Zhang Wan as commander with Li Shi as deputy, entrusted them with the elite of the realm, advanced and encamped at Yongbian, wholly under Commander Mao's command, to await the time for joint punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment I assumed provisional authority I dared not rest; I immediately appointed Envoy Zhang Wan commander with Li Shi as his deputy, entrusted them with the realm's finest troops, and advanced to encamp at Yongbian, wholly under Commander Mao's orders, awaiting the day for a joint punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 而適重兵在握，潛蓄覬覦，遂與龜城府使明璉舉兵內叛，直犯京城。

translations.literal: But Shi, with heavy troops in hand, secretly harbored covetous designs, and together with Myeongryeon, prefect of Guibu, raised troops in internal rebellion and marched straight against the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But Shi, with heavy troops in his grasp, secretly nursed ambitions of his own; together with Minglian, prefect of Guibu, he raised troops in rebellion and marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 晚收餘兵躡其後，與京輔官兵表裏夾攻，賊皆授首，而西邊軍實及列鎮儲偫罄於是役矣。

translations.literal: Wan gathered the remaining troops and followed in their rear, and with capital-area officers and soldiers attacked from front and rear; the rebels all lost their heads, but western military strength and stored provisions at the various garrisons were exhausted in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wan gathered the remaining troops and pursued from the rear; together with the capital garrison they attacked from both sides, and the rebels were all killed. But the western frontier's military stores and the provisions stockpiled at the garrisons were exhausted in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 毛鎮當全遼淪沒之後，孤軍東渡，寄寓海上，招集遼民前後數十萬，亦小邦所仰藉也。

translations.literal: After all Liaodong fell, Commander Mao alone crossed east with his army, lodged on the sea, and gathered several hundred thousand Liaodong people before and after—also what our small state relies upon.
translations.idiomatic: After all Liaodong fell, Commander Mao crossed east alone with his army, made his home on the sea, and gathered several hundred thousand Liaodong refugees—a force our small kingdom also relies upon.

sentences.zh: 顧以封疆多故，土瘠民貧，內供本國之軍需，外濟鎮兵之待哺，生谷有限，支給實難。

translations.literal: Yet because the frontier has many troubles, the land is barren and the people poor, supplying our realm's military needs within while assisting the garrison troops waiting to be fed without—income of grain is limited and provision is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the frontier is troubled, the land barren, and the people poor; we must supply our own army within while feeding the garrison troops without. Grain is scarce and provision truly hard.

sentences.zh: 遼民迫於饑餒，散佈村落，強者攫奪，弱者丐乞。

translations.literal: Liaodong people driven by hunger and famine scatter through villages—the strong seize by force, the weak beg.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong refugees, driven by hunger, scatter through the villages—the strong seize by force, the weak beg for food.

sentences.zh: 小邦兵民被撓不堪，拋棄鄉邑，轉徙內地。
